fields.essence: This is the energy of creation itself, the force that begins everything and is always beginning again. In you it makes what was not there before, in a shape no one else could have made. When it is moving you are more alive than at any other time: the work has light in it, something in you has to come out, and bringing it out is a joy. It arrives in its own time and leaves the same way.
fields.glance:
This is the energy of creation itself, the force that begins everything and is always beginning again. In you it makes what was not there before, in a shape no one else could have made. When it is moving you are more alive than at any other time: the work has light in it, something in you has to come out, and bringing it out is a joy. It arrives in its own time and leaves the same way.

In balance, this power has no fear of mistakes. Nothing new has ever been made without hundreds of wrong turns, so you begin before you know how it will end. What you are making will move one way and then another as it comes into the world; let it, because it has a life of its own. Your part is to be there when it happens, with a light hand, the way a midwife is there for a birth. By the time it is finished it has made you as much as you made it, and that is where the beauty is.

There are stretches when nothing comes, and they belong to this power as much as the making does. What comes next is being made in you where you cannot see it, and it needs you quiet, mostly on your own. Asking what is wrong with you is the one thing that makes the quiet last. Let it be, rest, and it comes back the way it left, all at once, carrying what it made in the dark.
fields.iching:
You are at the start of something, and the whole of its life is still ahead of it. Everything that begins passes through four seasons: it springs up, it grows, it is gathered in, then it is tried to see what it was worth. What you are asking about belongs to the whole cycle, not to this part, so look at all four from here. Nothing is yours until it has come through the last, and that takes longer than any beginning expects.

What it asks of you is to keep going, never to force. The sky moves through the day and the night without straining, which is why it never wears out. Make yourself strong the same way, a little every day rather than all of it in one blaze. Keep the pace of what is unfolding, slow when it is slow and fast when it is fast. Before you set out, be sure who you are and where you came from, because a force this size carries you a long way in whichever direction you are facing. The one danger in it is going too far. A strength like this can burn what it has made before it has taken shape.

In the body this energy is the head. Notice where you are holding yourself now: high, behind the eyes, already looking at what comes next. A beginning is felt there before the hands get any of it. Hold yourself the way the sky moves, steady and unhurried, with nothing in it strained. Heaven over Heaven: the sky, and under it the sky again, with nothing that gives way. Its creature is the dragon, which sleeps the winter at the bottom of deep water, wakes in spring, comes up into the open field and climbs into the sky. The traditional character shows vapour rising off wet ground under a strong sun, and the same word said another way means to parch. The Creative
fields.gene_keys:
Entropy Freshness Beauty Met, this energy is a fire, and what comes through you is alive the way a flame is alive. One morning the colour is back in things, and the joy has come with no more warning than sadness ever gave. With it comes something that has to be said or made, in your voice or with your hands. You take the step nobody has taken, and even when it fails you are out of the place you were shut in, which was the point.

Where it does most is a small room: a family, a few people who work together. Give it its moment and the whole room wakes. Then leave sooner than seems polite, because fresh things do not keep, and the one who lit the room can drain it by staying too long. The ones who carry this well are soft rather than hard, plain rather than shiny, because a fire is delicate and burns whoever grabs at it. Your strength is being able to be alone, trusting your own timing over anyone's. This energy goes flat some days, and the days go flat with it. You reach the end of one tired and cannot say what it was for. The word for it is numbness. Numbness is a feeling, though almost nobody knows they are in it, and knowing is most of the way out. You will do nearly anything rather than feel it, reach for the phone or call someone, and each works for about a minute.

Put a hand on your chest and notice what is there, even if it is nothing. Nothing is what it is meant to feel like at the start, so let it stay, with no pressure on it to change. It is not comfortable, nor is it meant to be. It is a gap, and a life needs its gaps. A bored child is not asking for a list of things to do, only for the blank to be seen, and you are the same. A fire begins as kindling that looks like nothing, then a breath on it. The flat you feel is the kindling, and your noticing it is the breath. Everything you look at is beautiful. A face, or a grey week in winter, shines with being exactly what it is, and the light is the same in all of it. It is so delicate that one word cracks it. A student once sat a whole dawn on a mountain beside his teacher, and when the sun rose he said one word, beautiful; the teacher afterwards called him a noisy fellow. The moment you say a thing is beautiful you have stepped outside it, so you say less and see more.

This is the fire when there is no longer anyone it is happening to. Even the flat days are beautiful from here, because they were part of it. All you can do is live it where people can see. Some will resent you for it, and some will come to stand in the light.
fields.human_design:
Self-Expression In the body, this energy is the pressure to make things your own way. Gate 1 is the door it comes through: the drive to put what is inside you out where it can be seen, in your shape and nobody else's. Nobody taught you the style. It is the one you had as a child, before anyone told you how things are done. When there is nowhere for it to go you are miserable, without always knowing why. When it does get out, the people near you feel more like themselves for having seen it.

From outside, doing it your way every time can look like stubbornness. What is going on is simpler: the making and the self are one movement, so asking you to do it the usual way is asking you to be someone else. The cost is that you are misunderstood more than most, and a hard word about the work lands like a hard word about you. People who carry this all their lives learn that being different was the strength all along, and that trying to be original on purpose is the one thing that chokes it.
fields.tarot: The making has gone well for once, and now there is more than you know what to do with. Ancestors Bloom holds that moment: a loaded cart, and plenty that keeps only while it is going somewhere. You belong with it, and what the family holds is one thing. What you were given cannot be kept, only spent. Here it is spent on the making, there on the handing out. Open it when something is in your hands and you want to know what it was for. One face from the Tarot stands near this strength, brought by its family.
fields.body:
In the body this energy is given to the liver, and the reason is spring. The liver is the organ of spring: it is the first to wake in the year, it starts the growing, it keeps the life in you moving through the whole of you. When the liver is at ease, everything in you moves. When it is tight, everything waits. It is also the part of you that plans ahead, the general of the body, choosing which way the season will go. That is the work of the creative force too. It begins the season and sets the direction. The liver is where the body does the same.

Of everything inside you, the liver alone can make itself again. Lose most of it to injury or surgery and within months it has grown back to full size, working the whole time. The energy that begins things was given to the one organ that can begin itself again. It sits under your ribs on the right side, about the size of a small loaf. Rest your hand there and you are resting it on the part of you that starts over. The spark you were born with has a substance in you, and the substance is lysine. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from meat or beans, or goes without. It is the same with the fire in you. On a morning when yours has dropped to a flicker, nobody notices you, and nothing you do by force brings it back. What brings it back in you is being fed, from outside and in its own time.

While it burns, everyone wants to be near you, and what you have then is a fire with something to feed. That is the same fire a season on, gathering a harvest round it, and in your body the two are made of one thing. Push it up by will and you pay, in what you give up to keep it lit. Fed, it comes back to you on its own.

fields.essence: Receiving is the whole of this energy, the ground in you that takes what falls and grows it. It turns nothing away. A seed goes into the same dark as a dead leaf, and the ground takes both. What has come to you is yours to hold while it becomes what it is going to be.
fields.glance:
Receiving is the whole of this energy, the ground in you that takes what falls and grows it. It turns nothing away. A seed goes into the same dark as a dead leaf, and the ground takes both. What has come to you is yours to hold while it becomes what it is going to be.

You can hold a thing as it is, without needing to change it first. Things come to you when you stop going out to get them, so your work now is to make room. What you do from trust leaves everyone with more. When you act from fear, everyone ends up with less, you most of all. The moves that matter are small and made by feel. From outside most of them look like doing nothing.

Some days you feel left behind and want to make something happen. Everything that grows comes out of the ground, and none of it is hurried. Stay where you are, stay soft, and let it come to you.
fields.iching:
You have been given something to carry through, and that is the whole of the work now. You did not start it, and it is not yours to steer. What it asks is the strength of the mare. She runs as far as any horse and still runs behind, going where the ground goes. Set out in front and you lose the way at once. Come behind, and the one worth following shows.

Keep to your own kind while this lasts, the ones who grow things and wait for them. You will lose the ones who charge ahead, and losing them is part of it. The ground lies soft until it moves, and then nothing is firmer. That is how you can be, and it goes well when you rest in what is steady.

Your belly carries weight all day, and nobody has to tell it how. It is the soft front of you, and it goes tight before you notice. Let it go, sit the way the ground sits, and hold what came to you until it is done. Earth over Earth is the hexagram of what you are given to carry. Earth is the part of you that takes a thing in and bears it. Here it meets the same ground underneath, where what came to you waits out of sight. That is why this hexagram has long been read as the ground under everything. The ground holds roads and houses it did not lay. So you grow a thing by carrying it, and you cannot hurry it. The Receptive
fields.gene_keys:
Dislocation Orientation Unity You find your way here by being carried, not by steering. The ground moves and you go with it. Things line up without your arranging them. The person you needed turns up, or you find you are in the right town with no plan behind it. None of it can be forced, because it happens while you are looking elsewhere. Your timing sharpens until being out of step shows up in your body as plainly as hunger. You start to look like yourself.

What it does for other people is the strange part. To set someone on their way you give them no advice, because advice they can get anywhere. You sit with them and want nothing from them. You let them see your weakness as much as your strength, and in your company they find out that being afraid is safe. You did not have to do anything. Harmony is catching, and a person who has stopped fighting their own life steadies the room. Somewhere along the way you stepped off the world, and you cannot say where. You stand on the same ground as everyone else, and it does not seem to hold you. You have been out of place in every room since. Most often it shows as busyness. The days fill, the load goes onto your shoulders, and your hands keep moving so you cannot hear the hollow underneath. The usual move is to change the outside with a new plan or a new town. The relief lasts as long as the unpacking.

You cannot step off the ground, and no turn you took was wrong. The feeling is real. What it tells you about your life is not true. It changes when you stop outrunning it and let it soak in, the way rain soaks into a field. What you were running from is a longing for home, and that longing is the first sign of the road back. You are home, and you know it. You stop looking, because there is no distance to cross. There is the ground and there is you, with no line where one ends and the other starts. Stand next to someone and there are three of you, counting the pair you make. Being home is ordinary, the plainest thing you know, and it holds everything.

Life goes on moving, and you are the ground it moves over, the way the seasons move over a field. Nothing is leading you now. You leave every mystery exactly where it is. You are back in the middle of your own life, which is where you have been all along.
fields.human_design:
Direction of the Self You feel where your life is heading before you have chosen it. Gate 2 is the name for that pull, and it sits in the middle of your chest. It does not make the road. It feels where the road already goes, and what belongs on that road comes toward you. A field knows which way is downhill without measuring anything, and you know your direction like that. If someone asks why you are going this way, you can only say that it is the way.

To anyone watching, this can look like waiting. Nobody sees a direction arriving, so they see you not deciding and call it drift. The cost sits somewhere else. You take it all on alone and settle for less than you wanted, because you did not trust that help would come. Let the direction find you, and let the help in with it.
fields.tarot: This ground follows whoever walks on it, and far enough along you stop knowing whose journey it is. It belongs to a family of two, the Ring of Water, and the other is Odyssey of Freedom. There you stop copying the lives around you and show what you are. Water always finds its way to more water. Open it when following has left you wondering who is travelling. Three of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, stand near this energy and no closer.
fields.body:
Everything in the front of you comes to one bone, the breastbone, which is why this energy belongs there. It is the flat bone down the middle of your chest, about the length of your hand. The collarbones come to its top and the ribs come to its edges from both sides. It goes out to nothing. It holds the front of you together by being the place things arrive. The ground works that way too, starting nothing and carrying what falls into it.

Every breath moves that bone, and the bone moves nothing. Rest two fingers in the notch at its top, between the collarbones, and breathe in. It lifts, then settles. You cannot move it on purpose. The ribs carry it a dozen or so times a minute, and they have done that since your first breath. Your fingers are resting on the part of you that is carried. Trust is not something you decide. Your body makes it slowly and lets it out while you rest. The substance under it is phenylalanine. You cannot make phenylalanine. It arrives in meat, eggs or beans, or not at all. Part of it is built into you as it came. The rest becomes what wakes you and moves you, then the colour of your skin and hair.

When you let something reach you, your body changes before your mind does. That is why you can feel held before you have understood anything. The further life carries you, the more people see who you actually are. Both of those happen on the same substance in you. The more you give way, the more of your own strength you feel.

fields.essence: Something new is alive in you, and this is the energy of its beginning. It has no shape yet, and it is already the most real thing you carry. You can feel how much is there without being able to say what it will become. That is what a beginning is from the inside, fullness and not knowing in one breath. Underneath, where nothing shows, a root is going down, and a root goes down for a long time before anything comes up.
fields.glance:
Something new is alive in you, and this is the energy of its beginning. It has no shape yet, and it is already the most real thing you carry. You can feel how much is there without being able to say what it will become. That is what a beginning is from the inside, fullness and not knowing in one breath. Underneath, where nothing shows, a root is going down, and a root goes down for a long time before anything comes up.

Carried well, this energy knows what the wrong turns are for. Everything that has ever grown began by pushing against something harder than itself, and the pushing is where its strength comes from. So the missteps at the start are not the cost of the thing but the making of it. What you have to push with is the store you began with, and it is enough, because everything this will become is already folded inside it. Keep the moves small and let them be rough. A small move made now holds.

The hard part is the pull to hurry. Not knowing what this will become is uncomfortable, and the discomfort asks you to settle it early, to name it or plan it to the end so the not knowing can stop. Settle it now and you settle it small. The store you began with is for one morning, the morning the ground gives, and a seed does not spend it early on the way there. Stay with the small moves, and when the ground gives it will not be little by little.
fields.iching:
You have started something in a hard place, and the difficulty you feel is the difficulty of every start. The push is from below, the shock that woke the thing; the weight is above, a storm that has built and not broken. Between the two, what you have begun is trying to get its head above the ground, and the ground is hard.

What it asks of you is not to set out for the goal yet. Nothing large should be undertaken from here. Gather the loose strands of what you have, sort them, and twist them into one cord you can hold, because the disorder is only strands that have not been laid together. Then find the people who can carry part of it and give them real charge, since a beginning that is one person's alone stays small. Keep near you someone who knows this ground, and do nothing by force.

In the body the shock is the foot, the part of you that steps first. The deep water is the ear, which hears the rain coming before the eye sees it. Notice which of the two you are living in now. The posture for this hour is a horse saddled and standing still: ready in every muscle, going nowhere yet. Keep your strength in, and let it thicken until the rain comes. Water over Thunder: the storm gathered above, and under it the shock that starts things. Clouds and thunder fill the sky, with the rain not yet fallen. The traditional character draws a sprout pressing up through hard ground, with the root drawn far longer than the shoot: what shows is the least of it, and what holds it is below. Difficulty at the Beginning
fields.gene_keys:
Chaos Innovation Innocence Something new comes out of what is changing, and making it is the best feeling you know. Cut a bush down in a garden and within days something else is growing in the space; that is this energy in you. You can work while the ground moves. You try a thing. Most of the tries fail, and the failing is how the shape is found. A child at play repeats one thing, a little differently each time, until something nobody planned appears, and you are doing what the child does. Mistakes are only changes with a judgement on them.

The hands that were holding are open now, so what is around you gets in and changes you. Other people's hands end up in the work, and it is better for them. What the trying needs is one fixed thing to turn around: keep the best version of what you are making in view and give the energy to that, because this much making with nothing to serve runs wild. You do not need to know the way there. You can love the work now without needing it to stay. The fear in this energy is that what you lean on will not stay. The people you love, the work you do: each is a hand holding something still, and somewhere you know that none of it can be made to stay. So the hands close. What you are afraid of is called chaos, and it is not the storm you picture. It is quieter than that, an unease under ordinary days, a low hum you stopped hearing years ago. A threat to one of the things you hold does not make the chaos. It shows you it was there. The usual move is to change something outside, to find a new thing to hold before the old one gives. That works for about as long as it takes to notice you are holding again.

The fear lives low in the belly as a tremor, and it asks only to be felt. Stay with it and it does not get worse; it opens. What you took for the ground going was something starting. Under the fear, the whole time, was love, and the clinging was only love that had not gone all the way. Innocence is what is left when you have lost what you held, more than once, and are still delighted by what arrives. The hands are open because there is nothing left to protect. A newborn has it without knowing; a very old person has it again, after a long search with a good deal of pain in it. The two are the same thing, and the only difference is that the old one knows. Nobody is in control. The child in you has always wanted to find out what happens then.

From here life is a play. You know how it ends, nobody knows the road, and the road is the play. You can grieve on the outside while underneath you watch the play go on, and the grief is part of it. Home was never in the body or anywhere in the sky. It is the feeling of love itself, and you are in it.
fields.human_design:
Ordering Giving a new thing a shape that will hold is the pressure this lens sees in the energy of beginning. Gate 3 is where it enters: the drive that takes what has never existed and finds the form it can live in, without which nothing new would ever settle into the world. In you it runs as an urge to get the raw thing into some order the moment it arrives. You try a shape, then another, and keep going until one holds. Where others see a mess you can see the structure that is trying to come through, and that is the strength. It is also why the process cannot be made to run straight.

From outside, the trying looks like disorder, and you may be called someone who starts things without finishing them. What is happening is that a new thing takes time to take root, the way a child takes years before it can be productive, and the waiting is where the doubt gets in. People who carry this all their lives learn to let the tries be tries, and that the panic to bring it out before its time is what burns them.
fields.tarot: Something ended to make room for what you are starting, and you feel the cost before you feel the room. You belong to a family of six. Between them they hold one whole life, and yours is the first breath. The others hold the watching and the cutting away, then the turn at the bottom, the feeding and the finishing. What the six share is one trust: whatever is let go finds its next shape. Open the one whose season you are in, to see that trust further along. Five faces gather here, one from the family and four from the weather.
fields.body:
The place in the body for this energy is the navel, and the reason is birth. The navel is the mark of the first beginning you ever made. For nine months you were fed there by a supply you did not make. In your first minutes outside, the cord was cut and the vessels closed on their own. From then on you did for yourself what had been done for you. What the vessels became still ties your wall at that point, one cord running up to your liver, two running down. Everything you have begun since was begun the same way, on a store you were given, before you could do it for yourself.

Press a finger straight into the navel and you meet something firm at once, the scar that closed it. Press a finger's width to either side and the wall gives. There is no muscle under your finger there, only the sheets from the two sides meeting, with the scar in their one gap. You are pressing on the place where you first had to begin. The beginning in you has a chemistry, one substance it shares with its kin, and the substance is leucine. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from meat or beans, or goes without. There is more of it in you than of any other piece you are built from, about one in every ten, so it is in everything you are made of, the hands as much as the heart.

Everything alive in you is changing, and what you are becoming takes with it what you have just left. In the body that is a fact about substance: what you will be is built of the same stuff as what you were, taken in from outside. The change never stops while you are alive, and the day it stops is the day you are not. While this energy is in you, the change is what you feel.

fields.essence: Something in front of you does not make sense yet, and you want to know why. The wish to understand is strongest when you are new to something, and it sends you to ask. Your mind does its best work explaining things, and it cannot tell you where to live or whom to love.
fields.glance:
Something in front of you does not make sense yet, and you want to know why. The wish to understand is strongest when you are new to something, and it sends you to ask. Your mind does its best work explaining things, and it cannot tell you where to live or whom to love.

Saying you do not know yet takes you further than acting as if you do. You will make mistakes and say things you later wince at, and that is what being new is for. Learn from someone who has been at it longer, and you add their experience to your own energy. They can learn from you too, because someone new is ready to change how things are done.

Some days nothing makes sense, and each answer you find only leads to the next question. When you keep changing direction, stop and take a breath, then go back to one thing. Understanding comes on its own, once you have had enough of answers and can live with the question.
fields.iching:
Something is in front of you that you do not understand, and you are the one who has to learn it. What you will become is still hidden, the way a seedling is hidden under the soil. You are ready to learn and do not yet know what you need.

This asks one thing of you: go and ask. Find the one who knows this ground, ask them once, and mean it. The first answer is the clear one. Ask the same thing a second time, then a third, and you have stopped asking. You are stirring the water, and every stir clouds it until nothing can be read there. Take the answer you were given and carry it off without another word. Then do the plain work well while the answer settles in you. A character grows out of small things finished.

Your hand and your ear are the two parts to use now. A hand holds a thing steady so you can look at it. An ear takes in what you cannot see. Hold still and listen. There is real danger under you here, the danger of not knowing, so stop at its edge and do not go down there alone. Mountain over Water is the hexagram of being new to something. Water is the danger in you of not knowing what you are doing. Mountain is the stillness that stops you there. The stillness sits above the danger because when you cannot see the way, stopping is what keeps you safe. That is why this hexagram has long been read as a spring at the foot of a mountain. A spring runs clearest where it leaves the ground and picks up dirt the further it goes. So what you learn right at the start of something matters most. Stop where you cannot see ahead, and you can be taught. Youthful Folly
fields.gene_keys:
Intolerance Understanding Forgiveness Understanding is what the water does once you stop stirring it: it clears by itself. It has nothing to do with knowledge. Knowledge is what your mind reaches for to take the unease away. The most it can hand you is the hope of peace, and that hope is what keeps you asking. Understanding arrives after you have looked at a thing from every side and found that each side can be argued. A riddle with no answer works the same way on a mind: the moment it sees its logic will never solve the thing, something gives. The answer comes up as a feeling in the whole of you, from the belly, and the question is done with.

Freed from the question, your mind goes back to what it loves, which is looking at patterns and playing with them. You see both sides of an argument and take neither. You understand people the same way. The restlessness is still in you, pointed outward now, at what could be put right in the world. Intolerance is a slant in your own logic. You have a bad day, decide you do not like someone, and by evening you have a list of good reasons. Underneath the reasons is a feeling, and the logic only measures what you sent it to find. That is how an opinion hardens into a certainty and a resentment into a conviction. You go blind with your own reasoning and cannot see that you have. Blame comes out of the reasons, then guilt, then a world split into sides.

Most people cannot sit alone in a room for an hour with nothing to do. They cannot bear their own minds. Under all of that is fear, thrown onto other people and held in place by an argument. Look honestly at the other side of your own opinion and you will find the fear it stands on. You handed your mind a job it cannot do, which is to make you safe. Forgiveness is a warmth that goes straight through the border between two people and finds no debt on either side. None of what happened was personal. The part of your mind that needed a reason for it has died. What takes its place watches the old story and does not pick it up. No restlessness is left in you. You cannot make forgiveness happen. It comes when you are tired enough of the drama, and it lands like a surprise. Something choked in your chest comes open. Then the forgiveness runs backward down the line of the people you came from, untying what they left tied. Debts that stood for generations are cancelled at their source. Water that nobody stirs runs clear, and anyone downstream can drink.
fields.human_design:
Formulization You are under a pressure to make sense of things, and Gate 4 is the name for it. It takes a pile of loose facts and finds the shape they make. It will not rest until something fits. You puzzle at everything and have to know how a thing works before you can leave it alone. You are happiest when a pattern closes. What it makes is an answer, and that is how the mind tries to make your life safe. Every answer is a guess that fitted. Hold it as a possibility and you can drop it the moment a better one comes. A mind that can drop its answers stays light.

A mind like this gets called a know-it-all, the one with an answer for everything. You can be wrong and sound completely sure at the same time. The pull is to act on an idea the moment it arrives, before it has taken root. Then you doubt yourself when it does not take. The idea was not wrong; it was early. Watch which of your answers the world goes on to prove, and let the rest go.
fields.tarot: Wanting a reason is what this energy does inside a bond, and it has to learn to live without one. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Union, and all four are about how you manage to be with other people. UL 7, Essential Nexus, is the guidance you follow in a group. UL 29, All In, is the yes you give with the whole of you. UL 59, Mystics Treasures, is the closeness that gets through your guard. This one carries the reasons people give each other. Five of the tarot's major cards stand around this energy, and most of them show you a way to learn.
fields.body:
The neocortex is where this energy sits in you, and the reason is youth. It is the thin folded sheet over the outside of your brain, the newest part of it in the history of animals. It is also the last part of you to finish. The front of it, where you weigh things up, is still being wired into your middle twenties. It takes in everything it knows from outside you. Your words come from there, and so does every reason you have ever given for anything. That is the young mind's work in you. It asks, it takes in, it holds what it was handed.

What this layer has learned, it cannot put down. Look at any word on this page and you cannot see it as marks. The meaning arrives before you can stop it, in a fraction of a second, doing what took you years to learn. Now try to un-read it. That is a first answer gone into you, and there is no asking it back out. The mind that cannot leave a question alone has a substance in you, and its name is valine. You cannot make it. Your body takes it in, from milk or meat, or goes without. When your body builds a protein it folds valine into the middle, away from water. The same substance carries a change this energy is making, from asking to understanding. A child born with that change already has a mind that does not run riot, from the first day.

The reasons you give for not being able to bear someone are made of that same substance. So is the closeness that gets past a guard. So is the yes you give with the whole of you. It is one chemistry for how people manage to be together. Without this energy there would be no reasons between you and anyone, no expectations and no blame.

fields.essence: This is the energy of waiting, and what you are waiting on is already real. This is not the waiting of someone with nothing coming. From inside it feels like a full sky before the rain comes down. In a life it is the space between the asking and the answer. Nothing you do in that space brings the answer nearer.
fields.glance:
This is the energy of waiting, and what you are waiting on is already real. This is not the waiting of someone with nothing coming. From inside it feels like a full sky before the rain comes down. In a life it is the space between the asking and the answer. Nothing you do in that space brings the answer nearer.

Wait without forcing it and you become sure of the thing. What you are waiting for does not come when you call it. It comes when it calls you. Waiting and patience are not the same thing, and only patience rests. Act from resolve and the thing comes at its right time. Act from hurry and the thing lands a beat off, however good the plan was. The pull is to check. You open the oven to see whether the bread has risen, and every opening lets the heat out. Bread rises in the dark with the door shut.

Let the hour come to you, and go on living your ordinary days while it does. There will be a stretch when it feels as though nothing is holding anything together. You will think the whole thing would stall the moment you stopped pushing. It does not stall. You are not the one holding it.
fields.iching:
You have done your part, and the thing you are waiting on has not moved. There is no weakness in that. What stands in front of you will not be pushed: a river too high to cross today, or a person who has not decided. The timing belongs to the sky, which takes no instructions. You cross the great water at the end of the wait, when the crossing is sure.

What this asks is that you be sure of the thing and stop looking for a sign. You can only wait this long for something true. If the thing you are waiting for is real, it stays clear to you the whole time. Keep to the ones who can wait beside you without talking about it. Eat, drink and sit at the laid table the way the wise do. The rain finds a rested person ready.

Your head and your ear are the parts to use now. The head stays up and clear while the rest of you sits. The ear hears a change before the eye sees it, so stop watching the sky and listen. Stand the way a farmer stands at his door with the seed already in the ground, under a sky that has not broken. Nothing about that is idle. The one move you make to hurry the rain fails. Every small move you make inside the wait comes good. Water over Heaven is the hexagram of waiting for what you cannot hurry. Heaven is the strength in you that never stops going at a thing. Water is the danger in front of you that no strength gets through. The danger sits above the strength because your strength pushes through everything but this. That is why this hexagram has long been read as clouds gathered over dry ground. The rain comes when the sky is full. The old character sets rain above someone stopped beneath it, made to wait for what only the sky can give. You are strong here, and the timing is not yours. Waiting
fields.gene_keys:
Impatience Patience Timelessness Letting a thing take the time it takes is the whole of patience, and you can learn it. Learning it takes patience. It is the one skill that proves itself: every wait that pays makes the next easier. At first it is a technique. You notice the urge to force, you do not act on it, and the unease stays a while. Then the loop that fed it goes quiet. Done often enough it sinks in. One day your body cools on its own, the way a mist comes off a river to calm a hot afternoon. Nothing has changed and everything is easier. From there you hear the rhythms you were moving too fast to notice. Winter comes in a life the way it comes in a year. It passes the same way, on its own, when it is let.

Once you stop practising it, patience is only trust. Life keeps a pattern you are inside and cannot see the whole of. Looking back, you keep finding it was there. The same slowing makes you kinder. Patience goes first and love comes in behind it. Impatience is a tightness in you that says everything should already have happened. The reply is late. The thing on its way is somehow too slow. It feels like drive and gets used as drive. What you begin from it lands a beat off, because acting out of agitation is never the same as acting out of resolve. Under it is a fear older than anything that happened to you, the fear that nothing is holding the pattern together. A body tuned to that fear never feels safe, whatever you arrange around it. Your breath goes high and shallow. The whole of you braces like someone late. It is a dry afternoon spent watching a sky that will not break, and the watching makes it longer.

None of this is a flaw in you. It is your own rhythm gone missing, and you can find it again. Feel the restlessness instead of obeying it and it sinks on its own. Underneath is the plain sense that life keeps its own time. You are inside that time, not outside it waiting to be let in. No one is waiting any more. The rain falls or it does not, and nobody in you is keeping count. Patience has gone along with impatience, because both of them need time to happen in. The hours no longer have any hold on you. Moods still come and go. The patterns that make up a person keep running, the way weather runs. You are still in all of it and no longer gripping any of it. This is very ordinary, quieter than the word makes it sound.

It is what patience becomes when even the one being patient lets go: the end of all fighting. Everything alive is waiting, and a life can be read as one long wait for its end. From here that is not sad, only true. The strength that stood under the sky is still there, and so is the sky. The rain is falling on the field.
fields.human_design:
Fixed Patterns You need your day to have a shape, and Gate 5 is the name for that need. It wants its meals at their hour and its sleep at its hour. It wants the same small returns every day. Discipline has nothing to do with this. It is older, from where the body keeps itself alive by doing the same things at the same times. In you it runs as comfort in the repeated thing, the walk at its time, the bed made before anything else. When your day keeps its pattern you have more of yourself for everything in it. When the pattern goes you feel it before you can say why.

From outside this gets called rigid, or afraid of anything new. What is really happening is that you are keeping a rhythm, and the rhythm is what lets the rest of your life move freely. It goes wrong from both ends, by forcing order on the day or by giving up on shape altogether. Keep your hours without apologising for them, and stop asking anyone else to keep theirs.
fields.tarot: This waiting is strength held under a sky that has not broken. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Light. UL 9, Ease in This, holds the same strength under a thin wind. UL 11, Sol Star, lets the ground come down to meet it. UL 26, Lighter Than a Feather, holds it under a mountain. What the four share is a trust that what is held is not lost. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the family and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The sacral plexus is where this energy sits in you. The reason is that this is the part of you that can hold something until it is time. It is a weave of nerves against the inner face of the flat bone at the base of your spine. Out of it run the nerves of your legs and of your bladder and bowel. Both of them fill on a schedule you did not set. This weave carries up the news that one is full, then holds it closed until the hour suits you. The engine that works you all day lives here too. It runs down by night, fills while you sleep, and is whole before you ask.

You are doing it now. Your bladder has been filling since you last stood up, and this weave is holding it until the hour comes. Put a hand flat on the base of your spine, on the bone between your hips. The weave lies just inside there, and your hand is resting on the part of you that can wait. The stillness this energy asks of you has a substance in you, and its name is threonine. Your body cannot make it. It arrives in what you eat, in eggs or beans, or it does not arrive at all. Beyond what it builds, it sets how your cells take light in and turn it into something you can use. How much light reaches you is set by how you live: fear closes it down, an open heart draws it in.

Three other energies in you run on the same substance, and it does the same work in all four. When you are in love the hours pass differently, as though you had stepped out of time. Patience felt deep in your body does the same thing more slowly. It opens your heart, and an open heart lets the light in.

fields.essence: Friction rises between two people the moment they come close. In you it is the pull toward someone and the flinch away from them, and both start in the same place. The flinch is no verdict on the person in front of you. It is the old fear that you can be hurt at all, and it wakes whenever someone comes near enough to matter. Every quarrel you have had began there, before anyone spoke.
fields.glance:
Friction rises between two people the moment they come close. In you it is the pull toward someone and the flinch away from them, and both start in the same place. The flinch is no verdict on the person in front of you. It is the old fear that you can be hurt at all, and it wakes whenever someone comes near enough to matter. Every quarrel you have had began there, before anyone spoke.

You learn to say the true thing at the right hour, and that is what the heat is for. A true thing said too soon is a stone thrown. Let the heat drop first and the same words go all the way in. You are not fearless. You have stopped being afraid of the fear itself, so it no longer decides for you, and nobody can use it to move you. From outside it looks like calm. Inside you are frightened, and you stay in the room.

The fear is older than you, carried in the blood from people you never met. Whoever stands closest only wakes it. Feel the fear in yourself rather than in them, and it loosens. Then the wall you built against them comes down on its own, because nothing behind it is in danger. The people you have fought hardest are the ones who bring you nearest to peace.
fields.iching:
You are in a dispute, your case is honest, and the other side has stopped listening. Your truth is real and the door is closed. Nothing you say now will open it, because the two of you are moving in opposite directions. Every push sends you further apart. Nobody comes out of the far end of a quarrel still holding what they wanted. A victory won here is taken back before long. So stop halfway. The middle of a quarrel is the only place in it where anything settles well.

What it asks for is a fair third person, someone with no stake on either side. Let that person say plainly what is being fought over, and it stops being about pride. Leave the great crossings alone for now, the move, the new undertaking. Both of you are strong and pulling opposite ways, so nothing large will hold. Every dispute sits inside a relationship, and you will still live beside this person when it is over. Hold firm on the inside. Give way on the outside, the way water does. Giving here is how the peace is kept, and it is no surrender.

The body's part in this is the ear, hollow on the outside so that something can get in. Check yourself now: are you talking, or are you listening? Sit the way water lies, low and open, and let what is said come all the way in before you answer. Heaven over Water is the hexagram of a quarrel. Heaven is the part of you that knows it is right and has stopped listening. Water is the part that feels wronged and keeps turning it over. The certainty sits above the hurt because being sure stops you hearing. That is why this hexagram has long been read as two natures moving apart. Two people can share a room for an hour and come out further apart. The old name sets speech beside the public square: a quarrel is what you kept in, said out loud. You are right, and being right is carrying you away from the person. Conflict
fields.gene_keys:
Conflict Diplomacy Peace You are tactful without trying, once the guard is down. This has nothing to do with the careful phrase, which anyone can learn and a shut heart can deliver perfectly. You feel in your body where the other person is, how open they are, how near their edge. A quarrel reaches you before it has taken a shape, and one word turned the right way lets it pass. When someone comes at you hot, you take the heat in and hand it back with nothing added, so the heat has nowhere to go. Refuse the game of blame and the other person is holding their own share, which either changes them or moves them out of your life.

Falling in love is the same motion: two natures rubbing until nothing stands between them. The people you are meant to open keep arriving, year after year, and each opening makes the next one easier. Being this open is the strength itself. Your heart is worn thin where anyone can get at it, and that is what lets you get at theirs. A feeling gets big enough and you stop having it, because it has you. From inside it the other person looks like the danger. That is where every quarrel starts: two people who have both stopped being anything but what they feel. Underneath sits one fear, older than any argument: that someone close can hurt you or take something from you. So you guard. Your chest hardens, and you keep a small distance going without deciding to. You learned that guard early, somewhere between seven and fourteen. Most of a life's strength goes into holding it up, and the cost never shows.

Think of the hardest relationship in your life now. What that person seems to hold over you is a part of yourself you would rather not meet. They are the only one who can bring it up. The fear is in you, not in them. Ask what the quarrel is really about, and the answer is nearly always the part of you they bring out. The people who will not leave you alone are carrying something you have not let yourself feel yet. That is why they stay. You have nothing to defend, because there is no one inside to be attacked. You used to work at keeping things even between you and everyone else. There is nothing to keep even now, and the work has stopped by itself. An old man rowing across a river was struck by another boat and turned to shout. The boat was empty and drifting, and the shout died in him. Live as that empty boat and nothing arrives as an attack. This peace lies under everything, all the time. Stop what you are doing and listen for it in the birds and in the wind dropping. Your own skin stops being a border, and you feel life moving in everything that lives. Nobody can take your life from you, because you are life.
fields.human_design:
Friction Something in you presses toward other people, and the rub is how you arrive. Gate 6 is the name for it. The wanting to be near a person and the fear of being seen arrive together, as one pressure. When two people warm to each other a heat comes up that does not feel like welcome. Most take that snag as proof the fit is wrong. It is the place where two feeling natures touch, and there is no closeness that skips it. The heat comes with the closeness itself, quick in some people and a slow simmer in others. Smooth it away and what remains is politeness with nothing under it.

From outside you look like someone who starts things. What happens is that you feel the edge before anyone else and cannot pretend it is not there. The cost is being called difficult by people who wanted the warmth without the rub. Live with this long enough and you find the rub was the way in. Where there is no friction there is no closeness either.
fields.tarot: This friction is the raw material, the thing that has to be heated before it changes. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Alchemy, and the other three go by the numbers on their cards. UL 40 is the will that holds a life up and refills in quiet. UL 47 is the old weight that becomes something worth having. UL 64 is the light that is there before it shows. What the four share is turning something hard in you into something you can use. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, to this one.
fields.body:
The belly knows first, and that is why this energy is given to the net of nerves over your gut. A feeling of yours is there before it is a thought. Your gut has a nerve system of its own, with more cells in it than your spine has. The great nerve running up to your brain carries news upward more than orders down, so the belly reports before the head decides. Under threat these nerves slow the gut and pull blood toward the muscles. That is the drop or the knot you feel in an argument before a word is said. It passes, and it is not a verdict.

Bring to mind someone you have been avoiding, and the belly answers before the thought is finished. Then breathe out slowly, a hand laid flat below your ribs, and feel the same place let go. The nerves that tightened it are the ones that release it when your breath lengthens. Your hand rests on the part of you that felt it first. When the last wall in you goes, the body follows, and every cell makes peace with the rest. That peace has a substance in you, and its name is glycine. It is the smallest of the twenty pieces every part of you is built from. Your body makes some and takes in more from food, from meat or from the bones a soup is boiled on. On the tongue it tastes sweet. It has been found in the dust of a comet, one of the few pieces of you ever picked up out there.

The friction in you shares this substance with three of its kin. Together they take what is raw in you and heat it until it changes. That happens in a body first, in the belly. Then it spreads, one opening making the next, out into the people around you.

fields.essence: Gathering is what this energy does. It takes people who are scattered and makes them one body that moves together. It is the reason a room settles when you walk into it. People listen to you even when they dislike what they hear. Your voice carries the sound of someone who can see where a thing is going. It does not push. You feel it as influence long before anyone would call it leading. It is in you whether or not you ever stand at the front.
fields.glance:
Gathering is what this energy does. It takes people who are scattered and makes them one body that moves together. It is the reason a room settles when you walk into it. People listen to you even when they dislike what they hear. Your voice carries the sound of someone who can see where a thing is going. It does not push. You feel it as influence long before anyone would call it leading. It is in you whether or not you ever stand at the front.

You gather people best by listening more than you speak. The greatest guides are the ones who listen. Someone who has been heard properly often finds their own answer with nothing added. Guide when you are asked, and take your time before you answer. Sometimes the best guidance is none. What you want for the people around you is that they need you less. A false leader holds on to you. A true one is quietly working to be rid of you, so that you can lead yourself.

The pull is toward being seen, and you do your work unseen. That is the hardest part of carrying this. Thanks come late or never, because you are a little ahead of the people around you. A crowd rarely thanks the one who was early. Hold this well and being thanked stops mattering. What you gather comes the slow way, drop by drop, like water collecting under the ground where nobody looks.
fields.iching:
Scattered strength is being called into one body now, and the calling needs a centre. A crowd is not an army. Loose strength wins nothing and breaks whatever stands near it. The same strength, gathered round one person it trusts, can carry a whole country. Water is dangerous while it is everywhere. Held under the ground, it is what the field drinks from.

A seasoned hand at the centre is what this asks for. It wants someone with the years to know when to advance and when to camp. That person is trusted the whole way from above and stands level with everyone below. The army exists to keep the people safe and for nothing else. Raised for any other reason, it turns on itself. So the way to grow your strength is not to seize more of it. Be generous to the people, hold them the way the earth holds water, and the crowd gathers on its own. Two rules govern it. The end has to be right, and so does the manner, especially at the start.

These two forces in your body are the belly that carries the weight and the ear that catches what has not been said. Sit the way the ground sits over water, open above and holding everything below. Listen before you move. Earth over Water is the hexagram of how many people become one. Water is the strength in you that would spend itself everywhere at once. Earth is the part of you that holds people the way ground holds rain. The ground lies over the water because strength that nobody holds spills everywhere and does nothing. That is why this hexagram has long been read as an army. An army is a crowd that moves as one body behind someone it trusts. Its old name means a heap turned into one working thing. You gather people by being the ground under them, never by pushing them. The Army
fields.gene_keys:
Division Guidance Virtue Guidance is help that does not impose. It never walks in uninvited. It never presses an answer on someone who only wanted to be heard. Its whole art is helping a person find their own road rather than taking the road over. Put your own opinions aside and listen. Sit with someone over tea and talk about ordinary things. What they needed arrives out of the space between you.

Carried like this, you lead from behind the throne rather than on it. You shape the way a room is going rather than telling the people in it what to do. You make a space where they find their own order, then step back and let someone else have the light. People feel clearer about their own direction just from being near you, without your saying a word. What holds it together is trust in life to go where it is going, rather than taking hold of it. Division is the line that puts some people above others, and it runs so deep that it looks like the shape of the world. It sorts everyone into classes and sides, then teaches each side to think in those sorts. After that nobody can picture another arrangement. Some are raised to follow and hand their authority to whoever sounds certain. Others are raised to take that authority and hold on to it. Both halves serve the same line, and the fear of losing power keeps it in place. Like draws like here. Stand at the level of someone waiting to be rescued, and you draw the leader who profits from keeping you there. Most of the people paid to help, the doctors and the teachers, would be out of work if you stopped needing them. Some part of them knows it.

There is nothing wrong with looking up to someone. It is a natural stage. The trick is to find the one who can truly listen. That person takes in what you carry so completely that you dare to feel it at last. Once you have felt it, what you were carrying loosens its hold. Virtue is what is best in a person, out in the open air, with nothing in them bent. It has nothing to do with being good on purpose, which anyone can perform. It is your own nature going through you unimpeded, and its reward is itself. That reward is past being seen and past being useful. It is delicate, and it cannot breathe where people speak ill of each other. Every day people do small unseen acts of it, and the power of those acts is past counting. Those acts are what holds the chaos off. An old story says the world is made of the shards of a vessel that broke, and each act sets one shard back. Seen from there, the whole long history of rank is a world waiting to be put back together. A child raised among people like this needs no other teaching.
fields.human_design:
Collaboration Organising other people is what this pull does, and Gate 7 is its name. It works almost without your trying. Put you among scattered people and within the hour they have a shape, without your having stood up. What you carry is the sense of where the whole thing is trying to go. With it comes the knack for seeing what each person is for, so the effort turns into one line of march. You are strongest beside the one at the front, directing the energy and holding the thing together. A leader is only as strong as what stands behind them.

Seen from outside, this can look like control, or like a person who cannot take a suggestion. The cost runs inward. Pushed toward the spotlight, this pull drains you, because being seen is not what it is for. Carry it for years and you learn that influence from beside is worth more than a title. A room follows the one who knows where they stand.
fields.tarot: This energy puts people in an order so that they can act as one, and that is not yet a bond. It belongs to a family of four called the Ring of Union. UL 4 is the mind that wants a reason for everything it feels. UL 29 is the yes given whole, and UL 59 is the closeness that gets past a guard. Between them the four hold how people manage to be together. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, near this energy.
fields.body:
The diaphragm is where this energy lives, and the reason is the breath. It is a dome of muscle across your middle. Every breath you take begins there. It tightens and drops, and the whole of you moves. The lungs fill, the belly rises, and blood is drawn toward the heart. One muscle in the middle moves, unseen, and the rest of you follows. That is what this energy does with people. Breathing low, everything in you is gathered round one centre. When the breath climbs high in the chest, the middle of you is straining and the rest comes apart around it.

It runs without an order, twenty thousand times a day, and takes one when you give it. Hold your breath and you have commanded it. Let go and it leads you again on its own. Put a hand on your belly and breathe in. The belly comes out under your hand, and nothing in the belly does that. You are feeling the one in the middle that the rest of you follows. Guidance has a substance in you, and the substance is valine. You cannot make it. Your body takes it in from meat or beans, or goes without. The muscle you move with takes it apart for itself instead of sending it to the liver. The same substance is in the forgiving in you and in the yes that goes all the way in. It is in the closeness that gets past whatever two people keep between them. One chemistry runs all of them, and it is for people with nothing ranked between them.

Guidance arrives when you pause with someone and are truly together. While you sit like that, your body is already in it, below any plan to help. A leadership shared between people is what this substance is for.

fields.essence: Being yourself among other people is the energy here. Most lives around you look alike, the same shape of week, the same wants. You learned to match them before you were seven, when fitting in kept you safe. Nobody can copy what you are underneath, because it comes out without a plan. It is the whole of what you have to give, and it is enough.
fields.glance:
Being yourself among other people is the energy here. Most lives around you look alike, the same shape of week, the same wants. You learned to match them before you were seven, when fitting in kept you safe. Nobody can copy what you are underneath, because it comes out without a plan. It is the whole of what you have to give, and it is enough.

You are not carrying an idea of what sort of person you are. You do not decide to be different, and you do not set out to fit. You live an ordinary life and still nobody mistakes you for anyone else. What comes out of you then is fresh, because you never planned it. People feel it more than they see it, in how you carry yourself and in the sound of your voice.

Think of a voice you know across a crowded room. You turn toward it before you have made out a word. That is how the people who are yours find you, by the sound of you being yourself. The moment you play a part, it stops working. So being seen is what you fear and the only thing that works.
fields.iching:
People come toward you, or you go to them, and the pull is real. Underneath it a quieter sorting goes on, and each kind settles beside its own. Nobody builds this; you recognise it. Before you join anything, ask yourself three things and answer honestly. Is what you bring big enough, will it last, will it hold? If it will, you have nothing to answer for. The ones with no settled place will come to you from every side. They arrive one at a time, as they each make up their minds.

Force nobody and delay nothing. Whoever comes too late finds the door shut, and that is the one hard edge in a gentle time. If you are the one keeping people together, you do it from underneath, the way the ground carries water. The people standing on you lend you that strength. Start pulling at them and it goes. Keep to the kind who come of their own accord. Pass on whatever comes to you, down through everyone, and the belonging lasts.

Your belly is the part of you that takes this in, and your ear is where it reaches you first. What you hear goes down into you and stays, the way ground keeps rain. Sit low, let your middle soften, and let what belongs to you arrive. Water over Earth is the hexagram of how you come to belong. Water is the part of you that goes where it can settle. Earth is the part of you that takes people in and keeps them. The water lies on top because the ground has to be there first. That is why this hexagram has long been read as rain on open country. Rain finds the low places, and nobody carries it there. Its name is a picture of two people standing close, the old word for a neighbourhood of five households under one head. So you belong to the people you let all the way in. Holding Together
fields.gene_keys:
Mediocrity Style Exquisiteness Style is what you are, flowering where anyone can see it. Living this takes a leap of faith in yourself. It has nothing to do with what you wear or how you live. Nobody can fake it or copy it, because it never passes through the mind on its way out. You are yourself without wondering what anyone thinks, and only other people call that a risk. Something creative takes hold of you rather than you of it. Once you have felt that freedom, whether it succeeds stops being the point.

It behaves like nature, which follows no plan at all. So anyone who keeps things running by rules finds it dangerous. It is wild, unplanned and full of leaps. So people push it to the edges, into art or music, where there is room for it. It does not need the edges. A person with this lives an ordinary outer life and a rebellious inner one. They walk through the market with everyone else, and you would still pick them out. Their freedom catches, and all they want is more people free. They stop dreaming the dream and start making it. Mediocrity is the fear of being different, and it wears the face of being sensible. You learned it in the years when sameness was rewarded and difference was corrected, and by now it feels like your own temperament. It is a stereotype you have worn so long that it keeps you safe. It keeps everyone else safe too, about who they think you are. Under it you think what everyone thinks and serve the machine that was here before you. You keep the machinery going instead of adding anything to it.

What you fear is not failing. It is succeeding, because becoming what you are would mean stepping past everything expected of you. You do not know who you would be out there. So you dream about the lives you might have had, watching other people live them on a screen, moved and going nowhere. Every child gives off a light, and yours went dim so gradually that you never caught the day it happened. You have fallen in love with what you are, and it is not vanity. Everywhere you look you see the same thing in other people, each one a diamond cut differently. Your nature is wild, and nothing tames it. You are never the same from one moment to the next, as fleeting as light through clouds. You lead nobody and leave no tracks to follow. The only strangers you know are the people who spend their lives copying someone else. They have become strangers to themselves. Water is weak, so nothing sticks to it, no plan and no grudge. You can rest completely, and resting is the last rebellion. A star at dawn and a bubble in a stream are gone while you look at them. So is all of this, and that is what makes it exquisite.
fields.human_design:
Contribution Something in you wants to add itself to the world and have it count. Gate 8 is the name for that pull. It is the urge to bring what only you see out where other people can use it, in your own words. With it comes the pressure to know when. Not every room wants it, and some ideas land nowhere. So you learn the hard way when to speak and when to keep the thing to yourself. What you are contributing in the end is yourself.

To other people it looks like someone who sets the fashion and does not mind standing apart. What is really going on is quieter. They cannot be anyone but themselves without the throat closing. The cost is being misunderstood by people who wanted them to fit, and the loneliness that follows. Trying to be a model for others, by becoming someone they are not, is the one thing that wears them out.
fields.tarot: This self of yours shows most clearly when you stop holding a shape. It belongs to a family of two called the Ring of Water, and the other is UL 2, the open ground that receives everything. These are the two great feminine codes in the genome. One takes in whatever falls on it, the other shines by its own nature, and the same chemistry runs through both. Open it when showing yourself has started to feel like work. Its family and its two trigrams bring five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, near this energy.
fields.body:
Of every organ, this energy is given to the thyroid, and the reason is the pace. Everything in you keeps one time, the warmth of your skin and the beat of your heart at rest. One small gland low in your neck sets that time, and it reaches every cell in you. It is two halves held as one by a bridge across your windpipe, about the weight of four coins.

You can feel that setting on a cold morning, in the warmth of your own hands, which is partly this gland's doing. It is in the sound of your voice too, in the timbre nobody else has. Rest two fingers on the inside of your wrist and count. Fear can hurry that beat in a second, but the pace it settles back to was set weeks ago, here in your neck. The self in you that nobody can copy has a substance, and its name is phenylalanine. Twenty small pieces build every protein in you, and this is one of them. Your body cannot make it, so it has to arrive in your food, in eggs or beans. Once inside you it turns into the pigment that colours your eyes. It also becomes the hormone that sets your pace.

Deep in you this substance works with a second one, and the two of them draw you toward people unlike you. The push and pull inside you is settled down there, below anything you decide. You change from one day to the next while the same substance goes in and burns away. A river is never the same water and is still the river.

keywords: Held by a Breath of Wind

fields.essence: This energy is the small step, with a great deal of power behind it. There is more strength in you than the day asks for, and the whole art of this is where you point it. Pointed at nothing it runs in a circle. Pointed at one thing you care about, it goes further than any great effort could, one plain step after another. In a life this is the long stretch made of small acts, the errands, the same tasks every day, which either add up or do not.
fields.glance:
This energy is the small step, with a great deal of power behind it. There is more strength in you than the day asks for, and the whole art of this is where you point it. Pointed at nothing it runs in a circle. Pointed at one thing you care about, it goes further than any great effort could, one plain step after another. In a life this is the long stretch made of small acts, the errands, the same tasks every day, which either add up or do not.

In a life that holds it well, it becomes a track worn by repetition. Do a thing with your heart in it, then do it again, and a groove forms that the rest of your life begins to run down on its own. Every act counts, however small, because each one makes more of whatever it was done from: an act done in resentment makes resentment, an act done in joy makes joy. When the small acts lead toward the one thing you want, even the chores stop being empty, since each is a step on the way. Without that one thing, the steps are decided by whoever is nearest, and you follow the crowd without meaning to.

Everything turns on where you look. Look up at the whole mountain and the knees go weak. Look down at your feet, and one step is small enough to take, with the next one easier. At every real beginning, a new year, a new house, the first few steps set the groove for all the rest, so take them with the thing you want held close.
fields.iching:
A great force in you is being held by something far smaller than itself. The strength is real and wants to go, while the only thing shaping it is a breath of wind across the top, too light to stop it if it chose to break through. So the holding here is gentle, and it works by patience, by friendliness, by many small things kept, never by a show of power. The old king in this picture kept neighbours who wanted war calm by a steady stream of friendliness.

The clouds have thickened and it has not rained. Everything needed is present, the charge is high, and still it does not fall, because the moment has not come; forced, it would scatter. What this asks is to attend to the small. Tend the details that serve the larger thing, keep the outward things in order, your manner, the way the day is kept, and let the rest go. Be the shepherd who keeps a flock calm by the calm of their own mind, letting the sheep find their own grass, watching only that they are safe.

In the body this energy is the thighs under the head, the strength that walks, checked by what is thought above it. A warning is folded into the gentleness. Do not fall in love with the small advantage, because if small gains are all you take pleasure in, they are all you will have. Keep to the small with the great in view. When the rain comes, the holding is over. Wind over Heaven: the sky's own strength moves below, and across the top of it passes a breath of wind, not stopping it, only shaping where it goes. Clouds have thickened over the western fields and no rain has fallen. The old character for the name puts a field under stored grass with a cover over it: a small store, kept. Small Taming
fields.gene_keys:
Inertia Determination Invincibility Determination is one step, taken. The mind shows you the whole mountain at once and the knees go weak just looking, so you stop looking up. You look down at your feet, and there is a stone to step onto. That first step is the hardest, and it is also the easiest, because it is only one step. Every step after it is easier, and if you fall off the path, the first step is what brings you back. The stones lead off over the horizon now; you cannot see where, and it does not matter, because they are leading somewhere.

The word sounds like force, gritted teeth, a long war of will, and it is closer to the opposite. The more of it you have, the less effort it asks, because what you are building is a groove: a thing done with heart, then done again, until the energy of your life follows the track on its own. By then the practice seems to hold itself up. Only the first few steps ask for real strength. Small acts done with heart gather a momentum that stops being stoppable, and one morning you are halfway up without having noticed the climb. The small has got hold of you, and this is what it is like. A path of stepping-stones runs in a circle, and you look down at each stone as you take it, careful, attentive, never noticing that the footprints you are stepping into are yesterday's. The errands and the small things that do not matter drink your life a sip at a time. You stay busy, believing you are taking steps, when every step lands you back where you began. Enthusiasm goes first, then the energy, then each feeds the loss of the other, and what is left goes into complaining, out loud or under your breath. Looked at from inside the circle, the mountain is far too high, the knees go weak, and the question of what the point is arrives on time.

The mountain is not the trouble; the looking up is. A dull task is rarely the wrong task. It means the thread back to what you cared about has gone slack. The thread can be picked up again in one act, which resets the direction of every step after it. Invincibility is in the weak, not the strong. The word sounds like an angel with a sword, and the thing is a child, soaked to the knees, running into a field of golden mist because she asked if she could. Nothing that delicate can be defeated, because there is nothing in it to defeat; what has let go of its edges is defenceless and unbeatable at once. The one force that works this way is love, which knows only giving, so it is never emptied.

The smaller a thing becomes, the more is packed inside it, until the very small opens into the boundless. All that ever was can sit in a palm, the size of a hazelnut, and the step you are taking is that small. Light brought to one point burns through anything, which is why a person living here can be hard to stand near: it lights up whatever you hoped not to see.
fields.human_design:
Focus Aiming is what this energy does in the body, and Gate 9 is the door it comes through: the drive to bring a great deal of power to bear on a very small point. The power underneath is real and wide; the gift is not in having it but in choosing where it lands. In you it is the pull to narrow down, to find the few details that serve the larger thing, letting the rest fall away. When it is on you can go for hours on one thing without noticing the room. It comes in waves, focus then scatter. It works best on one thing at a time; asked to hold three, it holds none.

From outside the scatter gets called restlessness, or a diagnosis, when what is going on is a focus with nowhere yet to land, spent on whatever is nearest. The trap on the other side is fixing on the detail until the whole thing disappears. People who carry this all their lives learn to hold the single step and the whole direction at once, the tree with the wood, letting neither erase the other.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Light, this code stands as the taming of the small. Its siblings, UL 5, 11, and 26, carry the rest of the ring's reach: the waiting, the peace, and the taming of the great. Bound by one amino acid, the four together work two of the highest themes a body can hold, time and light, the patient accumulation that finally turns boundless. Five Arcana gather around this card, reached by two separate roads. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Star, the quiet hope that keeps a person tending the small through a long darkness. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Wind above as the Wheel of Fortune and Death, the turning and the shedding; Heaven below as the Fool and the Empress, the first fearless step and the abundance it grows toward. The Star, the turning wheel, the shedding, the Fool and the Empress make one picture: a patient holding under a far hope, the strong force below learning to begin gently and to let what is finished fall away.
fields.body:
Every step you have ever taken began in the sacral plexus, which is why the body puts this energy there. From this weave of nerves at the base of your spine comes the largest nerve you have, thumb-wide where it starts, running down the back of each leg to the foot. Low in the same ground your body keeps its will, the part of you that goes on after the wanting has worn off. When your will is moving, the day has somewhere to go; when it stands, everything in you stands with it.

Walking is the groove already in you. Once you have taken the first step the rest go on without your thinking of them; the rhythm is made low in your spine and reaches your legs through this weave. Sit on something hard and feel the two bones you sit on. A little to the outside of each, the nerve that walks you passes on its way down, and you are sitting beside the part of you that takes the next step. The small step this energy is made of has a substance in you, and the substance is threonine. Your body cannot make it, so it comes in with what you eat, eggs or lentils, or not at all.
