The two trigrams each give their own faces: Thunder above as the Tower and Judgement, the strength that shatters and the strength that wakes; Heaven below as the Fool and the Empress, the pure beginning and the abundance it grows into. Taken as one image, this is raw power turning on the wheel of timing, breaking and waking above, originating and fruitful below.
fields.body:
This energy lives in your sacral plexus, and the reason is the belly. Power comes from the belly; pushing comes from the head, and you can tell them apart by where you feel them. The sacral plexus is a weave of nerves low in you, below and behind the navel, lying against the inside of the flat bone at the base of your spine. Nothing in you is watched less, and nothing in you is stronger. It drives the great muscle of the buttock, the one that holds a human being upright, it sends the largest nerve in the body down each leg, and it does all of it without asking you.

Stand up from a chair. The muscle that straightened your hip took its order from this weave before you had finished deciding to stand, and so did the muscles that kept your hips level while your weight moved. You did not do it, and you will not feel it. That is the power in you that no one is watching, and it is the strongest thing you have. The strength in you has a substance, and the substance is asparagine. Your body makes it for itself, out of what it already has, and asks nothing from your plate for it. The proteins that face outward from every cell you have wear their coat of sugar on it. When you are lost to the force moving through you and can hear no one, this is the chemistry at work. Left alone, the life in you runs fluid and cheap; every push against the way it wants to go burns more of you than the flow would have, which is the tiredness that follows forcing.

The strength that moves you and the knowing that breaks in on you unasked are made of one substance in you. The softest thing there is goes through rock without once pushing, and given its way the strength in you does the same.

fields.essence: This energy is hunger: the wanting that nothing you have yet has satisfied. In you it is the reach for the next thing: the street you have not walked, the face you have not met, the experience still ahead, wanted now, before the one in your hand is finished. It is the part of you that cannot leave life alone, the appetite under everything you would call progress. Whatever you hold, some of you is already looking past it, and that looking is what moves you.
fields.glance:
This energy is hunger: the wanting that nothing you have yet has satisfied. In you it is the reach for the next thing: the street you have not walked, the face you have not met, the experience still ahead, wanted now, before the one in your hand is finished. It is the part of you that cannot leave life alone, the appetite under everything you would call progress. Whatever you hold, some of you is already looking past it, and that looking is what moves you.

This hunger is sweet as long as you sip it and do not swallow it. It can be savoured and drawn out. It is what makes you human, and what brings people to one table. It does not need a far country. A circle half a mile wide around your own door holds more than one life can get through, provided you meet the same street as new each time. It is new; even the sky over it has moved since yesterday. What goes stale is the looking, not the world, and looking kept fresh makes an ordinary morning something you taste.

Take the hunger to the edge and stop there, the way a glass of wine is best a sip short of too much, so that a smile from someone you love is what tips you over. Keep a little hunger back. A little of it is your backbone; too much you pay for, in tiredness and in wanting more. In a hard stretch the hunger and your impatience feed each other, wanting it now, then wanting the next thing sooner, until nothing you reach for is tasted at all. You will overshoot more times than you can count. Be as forgiving of that as you would be of anyone else who was hungry.
fields.iching:
You are in the easy part of something, when the light is coming up and the way ahead is clear. What you set going is growing on its own now, the way young plants grow in full sun, and other people can see it. This is the season when you are wanted. The old picture is a lord at ease, given horses by his king in great number, called in to see him three times in one day, so well liked that his company is wanted morning, noon and night. You did not seize any of it. Being received is the situation itself.

What it asks is that you rise the way he rose. He served the ones above him with loyalty, the ones below him with generosity, and that was the whole of his climb. Advance like a mouse, small and quiet, then take your seat like a lion. Be willing to change before you ask anything else to. The light coming up does not make you good; it shows the good that was already in you, so let it show, then brighten it a little every day. The one thing that can spoil this is grabbing at it, because a good run pushed becomes a chase.

In the body this energy is the eyes. Notice where your looking is now: lifted, ahead, taking in more than it did an hour ago. Hold yourself as the sun holds itself in the morning, rising with no hurry, lighting everything on the way. Fire over Earth: the sun, and under it the ground it is climbing away from. This is the sun just up, clear of the field and still rising, the light spreading further every minute until the whole day stands open. Its creature is the horse, spirited strength that keeps to the ground. The traditional character sets the sun beside a sign for reaching: the daylight world, spreading. Progress
fields.gene_keys:
Hunger Adventure Boundlessness Adventure is this hunger met: the same wanting with the door open, walked through toward life instead of away from it. The wanting that spilled out into the world turns, comes home, and what changes is you. What breaks the hunger is love, not a person who fills you for a while but the feeling of being joined to everything, felt low behind the chest. From there the frontier is inward. There is still fear in you; you have found a footing high enough to outwit it.

A life is kept in sealed rooms, the job that never speaks to the marriage, the belief that lets no new thought in, and one wall taken down between two of them lets the whole house breathe. Learn the name of the man in the shop; listen to your children's music. When someone begins talking in the middle of your work, stop and give them the whole of you, because that pause is where the strange things happen. Of everything in you this is the one place you have a real choice, and it is taken by giving with no price on it. Give like that and something in you settles. The low of this energy is a hunger that no meal ends. You eat, and within the hour the emptiness is back, faint at first, then not, until you are reaching again. You do not know what you want; you only know you want it now, and while you want it you cannot think about what it costs. So the reach goes out through the door, for food, for someone, and each fills you for about as long as it takes to notice you are full. Then the emptying starts. At that moment two mistakes wait: you hold on to the thing, calling it love, or you blame it for failing you and move on.

Nothing brought in through that door has ended it, because what would end it is not out there; a taste of fullness fetched from outside leaves you hungrier than before. What changes it is not starving it and not stuffing it. It is to feel, all the way down, how completely the hunger has hold of you. Seen whole, its grip loosens. The reach turns round, comes back in, and that turning is the whole of the way out. There is no door here, because there is no wall, and no one left inside to be hungry. The one who wanted is gone, and what remains has no edges. The mind cannot hold this; it comes apart on contact, which is the point, since it was never the mind that knew it. The heart knows no bounds; from here the word for love and the word for being aware turn out to be one word. There is no beginning to anything and no end. A child already knows this. To a child anything is possible, and so it is.

Seen from here the whole long hunger was love that had not arrived yet, reaching in the dark for what it already was. The wanting, the bored years, the frantic ones, all of it was this, felt through too small an opening. Nothing is asked of you now. When something impossible happens near you, it is not surprising.
fields.human_design:
Experience What presses here is the experience you have not had yet, and then the telling of it. In the body it comes in at Gate 35: a hunger for life itself, for the new place, and for the wisdom that only comes from having lived it. Nothing learned from a page satisfies it. The same road, the same conversation, and something in you is already looking for the next.

From outside it looks like inconsistency. What is happening is the drive doing its work, gathering what it exists to gather, and the wisdom comes afterwards, only from the wandering. The cost is the rush: one experience straight into the next with nothing taken in, until you have done everything and learned nothing. After enough has been seen, the appetite curdles into the certainty that there is nothing new under the sun, and you settle into rooms that ask nothing of you. People who carry this all their lives learn to keep meeting life as if they had not done it before, even when they have done a version of it a hundred times, and to choose the experiences worth their time.
fields.tarot: This code holds the Ring of Miracles alone. It has no siblings. Where every other code sits in a family bound by a shared chemistry, this one is an island in the genome, a single card that is its own ring. That solitude is the teaching. The thing stands apart because it is the door, the one place in the whole structure where a person can reach through and change the laws that bind everyone else. Strength comes first, handed to this hexagram by its codon ring: the courage that gentles the animal in us rather than caging it. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Fire above as the Emperor and the Sun, the order that holds and the light that gladdens; Earth below as the Devil and the World, the appetite that binds and the whole at last made round. The Devil holds the chain and the World holds the wreath, and this card is the distance a hunger travels between them once courage walks it.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the thyroid, and the reason is that nothing hurries it. The thyroid sits low in the front of your neck, across the windpipe, and what it makes sets the pace your body runs at. It is the slowest dial in you: what it makes lasts about a week in your blood, a change shows over weeks, and nothing done today changes it by tonight. Whatever the hunger of the day wants, the pace of your body was set weeks ago and changes slowly, by the same gland whose hormone turns a tadpole into a frog. The change you wait for arrives on its own, and you never catch the moment it happens.

Put two fingers on the inside of your wrist and find the beat. Fear can put it up in a second; the beat you find at rest is the one this gland set, a while back, and no amount of wanting hurries it. Rest your fingers there and you are resting them on the part of you that cannot be rushed. The hunger you were born with runs on a substance, and the substance is tryptophan. You cannot make it; it comes in with meat, eggs, cheese or beans, and of all the pieces you are built from it is the rarest. From it your body makes serotonin, the chemistry of having had enough, most of it in the wall of your gut rather than your head. The hunger and the being satisfied are one chemistry, made inside you from what is fed in, so nothing fetched from outside ends it. What would end it is made in you, where the hunger is.

It is one link in a chain your body makes for itself. What sets it running is giving with nothing wanted back; give like that and what follows is happiness, then a trust that the whole of your life is in order.

fields.essence: Crisis is the energy here, the moment the floor you were standing on is not there. It comes as a drop in the stomach before the mind knows what has happened, then as the news itself: the call, or the door closing. Something in you that was lit goes under. A great deal of a life is lived in that light without anyone else knowing.
fields.glance:
Crisis is the energy here, the moment the floor you were standing on is not there. It comes as a drop in the stomach before the mind knows what has happened, then as the news itself: the call, or the door closing. Something in you that was lit goes under. A great deal of a life is lived in that light without anyone else knowing.

You become human through this energy when it is left open after the drop. The mind can be overwhelmed, the feelings can be overwhelmed, and the heart cannot; it has no top to it, so it can take in the whole of what is happening. The one who has been shaken like this, more than once, and stayed open through it is the one everybody comes to in their worst hour, because nothing that is brought to them is stranger than what they have already carried. What you have been through is not a wound you hide. It is the reason people trust you with theirs.

The hard hours in this are the ones after the drop, when everything in you wants to shut, or to turn the shaking into a drama so that at least it is outside you. Neither is a fault, and neither is the way. Let it shake you. When you find you have closed, forgive it, then open again, as many times as it takes. What grows in a heart that has been opened this often is a tenderness that nothing can wound.
fields.iching:
Something corrupt holds the high ground over you, and what is clear in you is in danger for being clear. This is no time to shine where you can be seen. The light is not put out but put under, where the dark cannot reach it, and it goes on seeing from there. What is ending is ending, what is coming cannot come yet, and nothing you do hurries either.

What it asks is the hardest kind of holding on. Do the day's work, even the drudgery. Live among the others and look like one of them. Keep the light low on purpose, and keep it lit. Do not force the change: the push for it is in the air, the hour has not come, and a light shown early is cut down. The old text stands two men behind this: one shut in a walled cave for seven years, who spent the dark making a book of counsel for times like his own; one at a corrupt court, who played mad so the king would spare him and carried his sense whole into the next age. Neither won by fighting. They outlasted.

In the body this energy is the eye under the belly. The seeing part of you has gone low, under the soft front of you, covered the way the ground covers the sun. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Let the belly be soft over what it hides, keep the eye open under it, and wait for the light to be safe again. Earth over Fire: the ground, and under it a fire still burning. The sun has gone down into the earth at dusk, and the light that should be in the sky is under the soil. The traditional name is two characters: the rising sun beside the setting moon, the picture of dawn, brightness itself; then a second that means to wound, to level, to make a thing hide. Darkening of the Light
fields.gene_keys:
Turbulence Humanity Compassion Being human is what the shaking was for. Meet it openly, once, without the story of being its victim, and something in you graduates: suffering stops setting you apart, becoming the one thing you have in common with every person alive. Pleasure comes with pain here, always, and you stop waiting for a life that has only the one. What you get instead is the antidote to fear, which is living from the heart while the ground moves.

The people who carry this are the ones others turn to in their worst hour, because they have looked into their own dark and are still open. Nothing brought to them is too much. They speak cleanly, having dropped the idea that fate is against them, and they accept without complaint that they live in a body that will die. The skill is small, and it is everything: when something threatens to overwhelm you, the heart draws back for a moment, then opens again, with you still there. When you find you have closed, you forgive the closing, forgive whoever caused it, and open once more. A heart that has healed this many times cannot be wounded. Disaster could strike at any hour, and you know it, the way everyone knows it. Most of a day is arranged so as not to feel that you know. Turbulence is what is felt when the arrangement fails: the churn under the breastbone, the body braced for a blow that has not come. It is kept humming by the news, which is one disaster after another until the fear feels like the weather. It shows up most in love, where the wanting runs deepest, and a life gets written as one upset after the next. Some part of you prefers the upsets; a churning life at least feels like a life.

What overwhelms you is the fear of suffering, heavier than anything it fears. Every feeling you have is innocent, and the trouble starts when you fight it or hide it out of fear. This energy pulls crisis toward it the way a magnet pulls, and it will keep bringing you the same hour until you have learned what it came to teach. There is no life without this shaking. The only question is what you do with your heart while it shakes. Compassion is the fragrance that comes off a person after the storm has passed. It cannot be given; it is earned, on a road that runs through the worst of what a human being can feel, so it speaks in a human voice, not from far away. The walls of the self are gone. What another person feels is felt in you, their aches, their wanting, their faults, all at once, and none of it separate from your own.

Those who reach this go toward the places where the light is darkest, the wars, the poor, and they do not flinch, because they have been so low once that nothing can be that intense again. With the fear burned out, what is left is peace. The look in their eyes can open the hardest chest. It was in the shaking all along, a seed inside the turbulence, waiting for you to stop running from it.
fields.human_design:
Crisis This energy, in the body, is the hunger for what you have not yet felt. Gate 36 is the door it comes through: a pull toward the untried experience, the boundary not yet crossed, so strong that a known life comes to feel like no life at all. Its fear is not being equal to what it finds there. The nervousness it makes is that one, the sense of falling short, felt most in the body and in love. The pressure runs in cycles; the wanting builds until you leap, and the leap is often into chaos, taken because nothing was happening rather than because the moment had come.

From outside this looks like impulsiveness, or a life that lurches from one crisis to the next, and part of that is true. The rest is an explorer's wiring, sent ahead to find out what is dangerous and what only looked it, then to come back knowing. The cost is the leap made too soon, out of boredom, which throws away the reward of staying with a thing long enough to become good at it.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Divinity, this code carries the suffering that cracks a person open. Its siblings, UL 22, 37, and 63, hold grace, the warmth of the family, and the doubt that comes before the dawn. Together this family runs the whole passage of redemption, the dark night and the divinity found waiting at the bottom of it. Around this buried light the Tarot sets five faces. The codon ring gives the first, the Hierophant, the keeper of the inner teaching that survives a dark age. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Earth above as the Devil and the World, the binding weight and the completed whole; Fire below as the Emperor and the Sun, the order that rules and the clarity that finally breaks back into the open. What they hold between them is a light bound under the dark, keeping its shape, waiting for the sun.
fields.body:
The solar plexus is this energy's place in you, and the reason is the lurch. Ride an elevator that starts down, or feel a plane drop, and the stomach seems to rise before you can think. The loose organs of the belly hang on their folds, so when the floor goes they lag a beat behind you, and the web of nerves behind the stomach, the solar plexus, reports the lag as the stomach climbing. That web reaches every organ in the belly, and the pit of the stomach in front of it is where trouble shows before it is known anywhere else. So the ground giving way under a life is felt in the same place as the floor going under your feet, and it is felt there first. A feeling fought instead of felt ripples out from here as a nervousness through the whole body.

Check it in any elevator that starts down: the stomach lifts, and for that fraction of a second you are the part of you that has not caught up. What churns in you when the world lurches is chemistry before it is thought, and one substance in that chemistry is proline. Your body makes it for itself, and meat has plenty of it besides. It is built above all into the stuff that holds you together, the fibre in skin, tendon, bone and every healed cut, about a quarter of which is proline.

The shaking you feel belongs to a family in you. The same chemistry brings the most intense feelings a person can have, then the darkest stretch, a night riddled with doubt, and what it is for is redemption: you are purged by your own suffering, which is the point. Suffering is built into you to crack you open. Freezing when it comes is a thing you learned, not a thing you are.

keywords: Feeding the Ones at Your Table
Home at the End of the Day

fields.essence: Family is the energy here, the warmth that gathers a few people around one table and keeps them there. Blood has nothing to do with it. Any small group drawn together for something larger than itself becomes a family, and you are the one in it who feels whether the bond is warm or has gone cold. In a life this is the pull to belong somewhere, to feed the people you love and to be fed by them, so that none of you has to stand alone.
fields.glance:
Family is the energy here, the warmth that gathers a few people around one table and keeps them there. Blood has nothing to do with it. Any small group drawn together for something larger than itself becomes a family, and you are the one in it who feels whether the bond is warm or has gone cold. In a life this is the pull to belong somewhere, to feed the people you love and to be fed by them, so that none of you has to stand alone.

Family at a full table is the strength of leaning and being leaned on. You let people depend on you, depending on them in turn without shame, and together you stand where neither of you could alone. What you give from the heart comes back, more than went out, from a direction you were not watching, though only when nothing was expected in return. That cannot be faked. A present from the head always has a small hope tied to it, and everyone can feel the string.

Give to yourself first. Under this warmth runs an old fear that you are holding everyone up while nobody holds you, and a person carrying it gives the way a trade is made, one thing for another, then calls it love. Ask your own heart what it needs before you pour it out for anyone, and the giving stops being a trade. Then the warmth goes out of you without your pushing it, and reaches people you never set out to warm.
fields.iching:
You are inside a household, and the household is the whole matter. Something outside has hurt you or worn you down, and you have turned back toward the people who are yours. That is the right turn. The strength here is inside, not out in the world, and what happens under this roof is what will set everything beyond it right, never the other way round. So the one who keeps the inside is the one everything pivots on: the person who keeps the food coming and does not follow every whim out the door. That is not the lesser half of a life. It is the half the other half stands on.

What it asks of you is two things. Let your words have something behind them, so that what you say in this house can be trusted. Let what you do stay the same from one day to the next, long enough to be relied on. Keep to the ones who are yours, each in their own place, the older as the older, the younger as the younger, and hold that order kindly rather than by force.

In the body this energy is the legs and the eyes: the legs that walk you home at the end of the day, the eyes that meet you when you come in. Notice how you are standing now. Come in, sit down among your own, and let the warmth in the middle of the room reach you before you do anything else. Wind over Fire: a fire on the hearth, with the warm air rising off it and moving out through the house. What is inside makes what goes out. The traditional character is a roof with a pig under it, the valued animal kept under the same roof as the people, which is the old word for a household. The Family
fields.gene_keys:
Weakness Equality Tenderness Seen from the heart, nobody is a winner or a loser, and that is not a claim that everyone is the same. It begins inside one person. You are two at once: a sharp mind with a soft heart under it, the drive to push beside the willingness to give way. When one side rules while the other submits you are split, and a split person is weak. Let the two court each other, neither serving the other, and the balance you make inside goes out into every room you enter.

What you are good for is the weak place in a group. You land in the middle of a family or a few people who work together and knit the frayed part back, without taking it over. You hold a young tree up until it can stand, then let go, and it may never thank you, though somewhere it will always be grateful. Freedom is what makes loyalty: the one you let leave is the one who stays close. You are never too proud to ask for help, and you never lean on it past the point where you could stand. Friendliness is its mark. The low here is the belief that you are powerless, and it does not feel like a belief. It feels like a plain fact. You have looked at the part of your life that struggles most, the money or the one bond that never settles, and decided it is a dead end. You bow your head to it and call that being realistic. Most people would rather stay beaten there than find out otherwise. Giving in does not rest you. It wears you out with a tiredness that has nothing worthwhile behind it, which is not the same as being tired after work you were glad to do.

You have been walking on crutches you never needed. You needed them only for as long as you believed you could not stand without them, and the day you let them drop you find the legs were strong the whole time. Turn the saying over: the family is held together by its weakest member, the one everyone gathers round. The place you struggle most is where the whole of your life can be lifted from, if you stop hiding it in the dark. The way a mother holds a child is what this energy becomes, and it is not one person's to have. It cannot be felt alone. It moves between people, the softest thing in a room and the one nothing can stand against, because there is no tension in it to push on. A family is where it is made. On a bright morning in a market it can be seen passing from person to person through the eyes, when nobody is guarding anything.

It is nearer the surface than anyone thinks. Give people the right conditions and up it comes, of itself, in everyone at once. The thing in you that you were most afraid of is what changes you, once you let it be held. Soft as it is, nothing has ever beaten it.
fields.human_design:
Friendship The pressure here is to belong: to have a few people who are yours and to see them provided for. Gate 37 is where it enters, and what comes through it is loyalty, the wordless agreement between people who share a table that says we are in this together. Its fear is that your own needs will go unmet while you meet everyone else's. The nervousness it makes is about tradition: the way things have always been done in this house, kept because it kept you safe, and defended past the point where it serves. Feelings run deep here, so whatever happens to a bond is felt all the way down.

From outside this looks like softness, or like someone who cannot bear a raised voice, and part of it is true. You will keep the peace rather than have the hard conversation, so what is unsaid piles up. The rest of it is the actual structure a group stands on, the agreement everyone leans on without ever naming it. The cost is giving until there is nothing left, because looking after yourself was never on the list.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Divinity, this code is the family alchemy. Its siblings, UL 22, 36, and 63, carry the rest of the ring: grace under pressure, the long dark before the dawn, and the inquiry that reaches the source. Together they orchestrate the slow turn of a life toward its own depth, four codes that bring the whole human being home. A hearth burns at the middle of a house and the wind carries its warmth out to the walls, and the Arcana of this card sit in three seats. The ring gives the Hierophant, the keeper of what is handed down. The two trigrams give their own faces: Wind above as the Wheel of Fortune, the turning that moves through a house from the inside out; Fire below as the Emperor and the Sun, the order at the centre and the bright warmth that order exists to protect. The Emperor wants the house held to one shape and the Wheel wants it always turning, and a family is what goes on living inside that argument.
fields.body:
The warmth under your breastbone half an hour after eating with people is where this energy lives in you, and the reason is the meal. Behind your stomach sits the solar plexus, a knot of nerves reaching everything in you a meal touches, stomach to gut. When you have eaten, the blood goes down to the belly by a nerve that runs through this knot, so the whole of you slows and warms. That is the part of you that is fed, and it is the part this energy runs. The fear that goes with it is the fear your needs will not be met. The body knows the difference between being fed and going without long before you have said a word. When you have lost it with someone, a hand on your shoulder brings you back sooner than anything said.

Sit down to eat with people you belong to, and wait. Twenty minutes in, the hollow under the breastbone goes warm and the whole body settles, as if it had been told it is safe. The warmth that passes between people has a substance in you, and the substance is proline. Your body makes its own, so it never has to come from food, though milk and bread are full of it all the same. Let a stock you have made from bones go cold: it sets to a jelly, and the setting is proline's doing.

You are not the only one carrying it. This energy never comes through one person alone: it is the heart of a family, whatever the blood, and in the body it is one chemistry with the people who carry it beside you. You will not feel it being made. What you feel is the warmth arriving in a room with other people in it, which is the only place it arrives.

fields.essence: The fight in you is this energy, and it is older than any reason you have had for it. It is the thing in an animal that turns on whatever comes near its young, kept in you from long before there were people, and it is one of the reasons there are people. In a life it is the part that will not lie down: when something you love is threatened you are on your feet before you have thought, and once you have taken hold of a thing you do not let it go. From outside it can look like hardness. From inside it is the protector, and it has been there the whole time.
fields.glance:
The fight in you is this energy, and it is older than any reason you have had for it. It is the thing in an animal that turns on whatever comes near its young, kept in you from long before there were people, and it is one of the reasons there are people. In a life it is the part that will not lie down: when something you love is threatened you are on your feet before you have thought, and once you have taken hold of a thing you do not let it go. From outside it can look like hardness. From inside it is the protector, and it has been there the whole time.

A wall worth pushing turns this into strength with a direction. The whole difference between this energy at its worst and its best is which fight you are in; nothing else about it has to change. A fight without a purpose is the one that wears you down. You can tell which kind you are in by the end of the day: a real fight leaves you spent and glad, a false one only spent. Be honest first about where you are unhappy, since that is where the fight is going now. Then put all of that daily pushing into the one thing you always wanted, and the effort that was grinding you down begins to carry you.

The way through is a breath. Struggle locks you into a way of breathing that makes you forget yourself and makes you deaf, so you go on hitting the same wall with nobody home. The moment you take one breath, the pattern is broken and a space opens. The tighter you hold on, the harder everything holds back, and the answer to most struggles is found in the gaps between them. You do not have to know how to get where you are going. You only have to begin, and a breath is a beginning.
fields.iching:
Two of you who belong together have turned to look different ways, and neither of you is wrong. That is the situation: not enemies, estranged. Each is only being what it is, the way fire goes up while water goes down, and each has stopped seeing the other clearly. You feel misunderstood, and you are. The difference between you is the one thing that matters to what you are doing.

What this asks of you is small. Do not try to force the whole into agreement, because the whole is out of reach for now. Settle the small things that lie within your grasp, one at a time, and let the large one heal from the edges in. What you have lost comes back on its own if it is not chased. Stay in the company of others and keep your own ground while you do, since the one worth following is never quite like the rest. Man differs from woman, and both want the same thing. Under the difference you can see there is a sameness you cannot, and your work is to act from it in small ways until the whole can follow.

In the body this energy is the eyes over the mouth. Notice where you are holding yourself now: the eyes narrowed on the difference, the mouth set against it. Let the mouth soften first. Keep your eyes, with the difference they see, and give the rest a little time. Fire over Lake: flame climbing off the top of still water, the one going up as the other settles down. Two sisters live under one roof here, the middle one with the youngest, and their wills go different ways. The traditional character carries an eye, and its oldest meaning is two eyes that do not look the same way. Opposition
fields.gene_keys:
Struggle Perseverance Honour Give this force a fight worth having and it stops being a struggle while you are still in it. Nothing about the force changes; the fight does. The difference is between pushing against the flow of things, which wears you out, and meeting an obstacle, which is only the grain of a real task. You come alive against an obstacle. You are built to be in the thick of things, making the impossible look easy while you give it everything, and the odds against you are the part you enjoy. The stubbornness and the hardness turn to use once they have somewhere to go; you can win a whole battle without doing harm.

Then there is the pause. Every animal pauses for no reason; a fly lands on your arm and simply stops; winter is a pause. Let life call you to yours. A day with pauses in it is a day you were awake for. The people living this way are easy to spot: they are simple, they smile, they have made the leap into their own heart. Something in you needs a fight, and when there is nothing worth fighting it fights whatever is nearest: yourself, or the people at your own table. You know the shape of it from inside. The jaw is set, and the teeth are in something that will not let go until it gives way. The day begins with a list and is over before you have looked up. Struggle can free you or trap you, and it traps you the moment it becomes a habit. There is a great sadness under it, because the fight it is having is never the one it was for. Most of that sadness lands on the people you love, the love between you ground thin by two who have not found what they are for.

Here is what keeps it going. As long as you are fighting something, you are somebody, in charge of your corner of the world. Let the fight go and there is a fear that you would go with it. That fear is old, and it is not true: with nothing to push against, the whole of you is still there. Honour is what the fight becomes when there is nobody left who needs to win it. It is a place you stand rather than a feeling you have, reached by living your own truth, and at the far end of being yourself you are no longer apart from anyone. Combat turns into a dance. To honour someone is to hold them at their highest whatever they are now, so you can be lied to or used and never sink to it. The test of an act is whether it brought people together or divided them.

A wounded officer once sent the medic to his men first, and was dead when the medic came back. He was not thinking. The act outlived him because someone wrote it down. Every true act of honour goes on like that, told and retold, reminding whoever hears it what a person is. It is quiet, and it lights a fire in everyone who sees it.
fields.human_design: The Fighter Gate 38 is the pressure to find out what is worth fighting for, and what it drives you to do is stand up. It is called the Fighter, and the name misleads, because the pressure is not for the fight; it is for the finding. You question, you probe, you will not look away from a hard truth, and when something is wrong you say so, welcome or not. Other people's opinions do not move you much; this is one of the places in a person built to tune them out, so the work can get done. The cost, from outside, is that you can look stubborn, a person who turns every disagreement into a fight. Some of that is true. The pressure has to be spent, and a fight picked only to spend it is the one thing this drive warns you against. People who carry this all their lives learn to meet difficulty as a question rather than a battle, asking what it shows them about what matters. To the people near them they become the loyal one, the friend who is still standing when everyone else has sat down.
fields.tarot: Within the Codon Ring of Humanity, this code sets the pattern of all human struggle, the labour of form reaching for spirit. Its siblings, UL 10, 17, 21, 25, and 51, carry the rest of the human story: the conduct of the self, the opinion that follows, the bite that corrects, the innocence beneath it, and the shock that wakes. Together they hold what it is to be a person. Nothing keeps its disguise under the Sun's plain daylight, and this card's Arcana fall along that same clean line of division. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Chariot, the one who steers two opposing forces as a single vehicle. The two trigrams each give their own faces. Fire above carries the Emperor and the Sun, dominion and the clear daylight that names things apart. Lake below carries the Lovers and the Star, the choice between two and the quiet hope that heals after the fight. The arc they trace is this card's own: two forces yoked, divided clearly, and reconciled by faith.
fields.body:
This energy is given to the adrenals, and the reason is the fight. They are two small glands, one on top of each kidney, under the last ribs, and what they do is arm you. The core of each is a nerve that grew into a gland, fired straight from the spine, so when something goes bang the whole of you is ready in the same second: the heart quickens, the airways open. It does that the same for your wrong fights and your right ones, because it cannot tell them apart. Your strength is held ready before you have decided anything, and if nothing follows it stands down, over in a couple of minutes.

Put a hand on your chest a second after a door slams: the heart under it is already going harder, and nothing was decided. Keep the hand there a minute and feel it settle. You are resting it on what the fight in you does before you have chosen it, and on how it lets go. The struggle in you has a substance, and the substance is arginine. Your body makes it for itself, and it is built into every protein you are made of. It comes to you in meat, or in a handful of nuts. Every human being who ever fought their own lower nature was fighting with this in them. The pattern of all human struggle, the pull of a body toward something higher than itself, is set down in this one chemistry, and it is a chemistry you share with your kin. In you it is the substance of getting up again, since through defeat a person learns to be stronger.

With two others it makes the charge your muscle keeps ready for the first seconds of any hard effort. What you spend in the first push was stored before you pushed.

fields.essence: This energy is pressure, the charge that builds in you and has to go somewhere. It is the urge to act that is in you before any thought, and it presses on whatever has gone still, in you or near you, to find out whether it is alive. Life uses it on you all the time: something disturbs you, and the disturbance is life asking you to grow rather than wilt. Whoever winds you up is carrying it to you. It lives wherever a way has closed, at the block in the road, in the person you cannot get past, in the part of your own body that will not move.
fields.glance:
This energy is pressure, the charge that builds in you and has to go somewhere. It is the urge to act that is in you before any thought, and it presses on whatever has gone still, in you or near you, to find out whether it is alive. Life uses it on you all the time: something disturbs you, and the disturbance is life asking you to grow rather than wilt. Whoever winds you up is carrying it to you. It lives wherever a way has closed, at the block in the road, in the person you cannot get past, in the part of your own body that will not move.

Pressure with somewhere to go lets the provocation in rather than turning away from it. The thing that gets to you is pointing at a pattern, usually one you had not been honest with yourself about. The block you keep hitting is not a wall; it is where your own force gathered and stopped, with something worth having behind it. Every block is a breakthrough not yet made. The people who live this way become the unlockers, first of themselves and then of anyone near them, because they know from inside how a stuck thing moves. Pried open by will, it does not move; the pressure forced out that way tightens again, harder than before.

Let the pressure find its work. Let out by steady work it comes back as the energy you had as a child, which in an adult is called making things, and the more you make the more of it there is. The force that fights when it is cornered is the same force that makes when it is free. The only difference is whether it has somewhere to go.
fields.iching:
You set out and the way closes, so you try another, which closes too. This is the blocked road, and the trouble in it is not your fault; it is in the lay of the land, water above you, rock beneath, a leg that will not do what you ask of it. Forcing it is how you fall. What the situation asks is that you see the danger and stop, which is not weakness but knowing. Then go where the ground is soft, not up onto the hard rock. There is someone who has crossed this before; find them, and follow what they hold to be worth having. Stay true through it and it comes out well.

While you wait, the work is on yourself. Where the will cannot push outward it can turn round; the one who would grow uses the stopped time to look at their own conduct and mend it. Water does get through in the end. It goes down, finds the way through the depth of what stopped it, and does that by being water, not by striking the rock.

In the body this energy is the feet. Notice them now, cold or warm, set flat or ready to go. A leg the blood has not reached will not carry you, whatever you decide. Stand where you are, feet on the ground, and let the stop be the stop. Water over Mountain: a stream running down off a peak onto rock that will not move, danger above and a full stop below, with no path between them. The old character shows a foot and cold, blood not reaching the feet, a leg that will not carry you: a limp. Obstruction
fields.gene_keys:
Provocation Dynamism Liberation Let loose, this energy is the one that runs a small child: the crackle in the air around them, never spent, back the moment it was used up. Most of it was traded away by seven for the tightness you now call your character, and none of that trade is final. What comes back, when it comes, is not play any more but the same force grown up, which is creativity, and the plainest way to call it back is to do what you love; the more you make, the more energy there is to make with.

It is catching. In the company of someone living this way you breathe all the way down again, your horizons widen, and they never seem to run out, as if driven from somewhere past themselves. They do not wait; they begin things, spark them, push. There are grades of this fire: the one who fights because he cannot help it, the one who directs his heat where it is needed, and the rare one nothing can provoke. The release, when it comes, is closer to laughing until the body shakes loose, after long steady work. Someone knows the note. Your partner, or a child at the one pitch that goes through you, says the small thing in the exact tone, and something in you has gone off before a thought could reach it; the tone was aimed at the place already raw. That is provocation, and it lives in sound: it is almost never what was said. Under the heat is a colder thing, the fear of being trapped, of losing the room to act, and anything cornered will strike. You are trapped the moment you react. The one who pushes and the one who is pushed are playing one old game; most people play both parts, on different days.

Look at what happened. Someone made sounds with their throat, and a handful of tones sent you into a state you did not choose; the only reason it worked is that you took it personally. Held down instead, the same force stops the breath short, and you run your days on the top of the lungs, slowly worn down. Move house or leave the job and the trapped feeling comes with you, because it was never in the room. Nothing can provoke this. The word still enters the ear, the mind still turns it into meaning, and the awareness it lands in does not move; you hear without following the sound. To get here the one thing that seemed to fuel you, your own separate freedom, is given up. It feels like a physical death, every plan and piece of work surrendered into a single vanishing point, the tunnel of agony that turns, without fail, into ecstasy. What comes back is larger than freedom.

The ones it has happened to are dangerous to be near: they aim their love straight at the weakest place in your armour, using any means to test how far you have surrendered, and if anything still lands personally there is further to go. Under the water a dragonfly nymph, a perfect hunter, one day climbs toward the light for no reason its life could give it. Something inside provoked the leap.
fields.human_design: Provocation Gate 39 is the pressure to provoke, and what it drives you to do is disturb what has gone still, in a person or in a room, to see whether it is alive. Provocation means something more exact than trouble-making: you are here to needle people toward spirit, toward the knowledge that what they need is not going to run out, and you do it by teasing, playfully or not, until something in them moves. Timing is everything in it. Done when the person is ready it is an infectious spark that wakes the whole room; done only to let off your own pressure it is a nuisance nobody enjoys. From outside it can look like restlessness, a person who cannot leave well enough alone. What is happening is a search: the pressure is hunting for the place where the energy has stopped, because pressing on a stuck place is the only way to find it. People who carry this all their lives learn to be hard to influence, to use every moment of felt scarcity as a place to push off from, and to say the thing nobody is saying only when it will land.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Seeking, this code stands as the spark, the pressure that drives a person to look for the source of their own suffering. Its siblings, UL 15, 52, 53, 54, and 58, carry the rest of the search: the wide acceptance, the keeping still, the slow growth, the leap toward another, the joy that comes through. Together they are the family that cannot rest until it finds what is true. One figure arrives here twice. The codon ring gives the Hermit, the lamp carried inward, and the lower trigram gives the Hermit again, so the seeker's light doubles at the centre of this card. The trigrams round it out: Water above as the High Priestess and the Hanged Man, the listening and the held pause; Mountain below as the Hermit and the Hierophant, the inward search and the keeper of what was passed down. The Hierophant keeps the road already walked and the Hermit steps off every road, and a shut gate sends you to both.
fields.body:
The adrenals are where this energy sits in your body, and the reason is the rush. Two small glands, one on top of each kidney, answer a threat before you decide anything: within a second the rush is out, the blood has left your skin for your muscles, your hands go cold, a little damp, and everything in you is ready to move. It is real, and it is over in a couple of minutes, because your body clears it that fast. That is the work of this energy too: a charge that arrives in you before thought, has to go somewhere, and cannot be kept. A body that keeps calling for it is under a pressure with no way out, and from inside you feel that as a tiredness no rest touches.

The last time something startled you, your hands went cold a moment after, because the blood had gone where it was needed; when the rush had passed a deep breath came by itself, without your asking. That breath, not the rush, is what lasts in you. The urge to act that is in you before any thought has a substance, and the substance is serine. It is rooted low in your body, where the rush comes from, and it is one chemistry shared with the kin of this energy, each of which presses on you in a different way; yours is the gutsy one, explosive, all about action. It makes an enormous pressure in you and in the room around you; that pressure is what makes things: it is what drives a person past what they were.

A block is where the pressure in you has gathered, which makes it a place to look rather than a wall. When you are cut, the blood that closes the wound is turned into a clot by something that cuts with a serine at its edge.

fields.essence: The will is the energy here, the part of you that carries a life through. It lives in you as a spring, filling from underneath in its own time, giving what it has for as long as it is left to fill. In a life it is what you put into whatever you have set your hand to, and what returns when you stop. The water rises on its own when what you are doing is what your life was for. When it is not, you haul it up by the bucket, and hauling empties a spring faster than it fills.
fields.glance:
The will is the energy here, the part of you that carries a life through. It lives in you as a spring, filling from underneath in its own time, giving what it has for as long as it is left to fill. In a life it is what you put into whatever you have set your hand to, and what returns when you stop. The water rises on its own when what you are doing is what your life was for. When it is not, you haul it up by the bucket, and hauling empties a spring faster than it fills.

The spring that is left to fill gives a strength that does not wear out, because nothing in it is forced. There is one thing you are here to do, and it is probably in front of you now. Give yourself to that and the tiredness goes, because work that fits you is not work; the strength for it arrives as you spend it. You still work hard, harder than most, and you stop when it is time to stop. Help comes on its own once you are doing what is yours, and goes when you push against your own life or give in to somebody else's. Time alone is where this strength refills, so you do not need company to be full.

Do less. Where you spend too much only you can see: too much at work with nothing left for home, or everything for other people. Cut those one at a time, without hurry, because the hurry was most of the trouble; what is left settles the way the body does when it is given less to carry. There is a tiredness that a night's sleep does not touch, and it comes from being cut off from your own source for too long. Nothing you were made for was meant to be this hard. Stop, be quiet, be on your own a while, and the water comes up.
fields.iching:
The hard stretch is ending, and knowing that is the first thing asked of you. The storm that stood over you so long has broken, and the rain after thunder is the kind everything grows under: a hundred kinds of seed split open at once. Danger is left behind by moving, and you have moved. Now the way asks two things. If there is nothing more to do, go back: to the old ways, to what your days were before the trouble, without the urge to change everything because you came through. If something is still to do, do it early, in the grey before the day starts, while the strength of the storm is in you and before the trouble can set again. Do not stand in the afterglow; whoever came through this before you went back to work the next morning, and you can walk in their steps.

Then forgive. After a storm the wise let the rain wash the offence off, their own mistakes with everyone else's, because a person still holding on to who was to blame is still tied. Give it time; a knot comes undone at the pace it was tied. In the body this is the foot. After a long time sitting still, the foot is the first thing to move, and it moves before you have decided to walk. Stand up the way a field looks after rain, clear with nothing left clenched, and take the first step early. Thunder over Water: a storm breaking over a deep pool, the first roll gone through and the rain coming down. What was tied all through the waiting comes undone. The traditional character is a knife taking the horn from an ox, a thing joined being taken apart, which is the old word for untying a knot and for setting free. Deliverance
fields.gene_keys:
Exhaustion Resolve Divine Will Deciding is where this strength comes in, and the deciding is done with an open hand. Take hold of the one thing that is yours and the rest drops from your fingers: the commitments that were never yours, the things you did because someone asked. What stays is what feeds you, and you can work harder than before without wearing out, since the willing is built into the work. You know when to say no, and you say it without a fight, because whoever you turn away belongs somewhere else. When life calls you off in the middle, a child or a friend at the door, you put the work down for the hour; that is not the strength failing, it is the strength.

Most of this is knowing how to rest. Rest is everywhere once you stop giving in to too much: a walk with nowhere to get to, the work you love with the people you love. None of this is going without; you take what life offers, with measure, and sometimes more than you need. A worn-out person who meets you like this goes away changed. Tired is the low here, the kind of tired that has stopped being about sleep, and the hand is where to see it. Everything you have taken on is in that hand, and it will not open: the job, the people who lean on you, more than any one hand was made to hold. You live in a time that calls this normal. Doing more, holding on harder: that is what you were told a strong person does, and each is what drains you. The cost is felt as thirst. You are thirsty for something you cannot name, and most of the time you do not know how thirsty you are, because the hand is too busy to notice. Underneath, something is being denied, usually a feeling.

The way it runs you is excess: too much in one corner of your life, nothing in another, so that you are many things to many people and yourself to none. Cut off from what feeds you, you begin to run down, the way anything does that is taken from and not fed. The hand does not need to be forced open, only noticed, and that is where the low starts to end. Both hands are empty now, and nothing is missing. What was decided with an open hand is not decided at all any more, because there is no one left to do the choosing. You are free to do exactly as you please, and none of it is in your hands. That is not a defeat. It is the deepest rest a body can have, every part of it at ease with nothing pushing against anything. People who come near you can see it, because it shows in the skin like light. Nobody can pretend their way here; the ones worn out by searching who take up the idea of surrender as a way off the hook have only gone quiet. It comes at the end of the searching, when every hope has been dropped, and it comes alone. There is nothing to reach for outside your own aloneness.
fields.human_design:
Restoration Stepping back is the pressure here. Gate 40 is the door it comes through: the pull, after work or after people, to go off on your own and gather yourself again. In the body it is felt as a need to be alone that arrives before you can explain it, sometimes in the middle of a room with nothing wrong in it. Something in you has to go away to come back, and it goes whether or not you let it, so the choice is only whether you go with it.

From outside it looks like withdrawal, and a partner can read it as rejection unless you say what it is. From inside the danger runs the other way, toward staying: giving to everyone who asks, earning your place by doing more than was asked, blaming others for a tiredness you never named. The loneliness that comes with this is a signal, meant to be read as an invitation inward, not as proof of anything about your worth. People who carry it all their lives learn the rhythm of going away then coming back, and find they return with more to give than they left with, because they went.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Alchemy, this code stands as the one that turns exhaustion into surrender. Its siblings, UL 6, 47, and 64, carry the rest of the work: the friction that forces change, the pressure that has no way out, and the confusion just before the dawn. The whole family is named for transmutation, the slow conversion of the darkness each of them holds into its own direct path to grace. Storm overhead and still water underneath, that is the Tarot's picture of this card. The codon ring gives the Magician, the maker who turns will into form. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Thunder above as the Tower and Judgement, the shock that breaks the structure and the call that wakes the dead ground; Water below as the High Priestess and the Hanged Man, the one who perceives in the dark and the one who hangs still until the view turns right. All five together say one thing, a breaking overhead met by a deep patience beneath.
fields.body:
The stomach is where this energy lives in you, and the reason is rest. It is the part of you that turns what you eat into what you run on, and does that only while you are at rest. It makes room for your meal before the meal arrives, then works on it for hours, unasked. When you are afraid, angry or straining, it stops; the blood goes to your muscles and the meal waits. When it is full, the will in you is content; empty, the will in you goes out to find food. What you force costs you what you had, and what you take in at rest is what you have to give.

It lies high on your left, under the ribs, below the tip of the breastbone. After a meal, rest a hand there and you can feel the fullness; on an empty morning the growl under your hand is its wall working on nothing. You are resting your hand on the part of you that only works when you leave it alone. The will in you has a substance, and the substance is glycine. It is the smallest of the twenty pieces you are built from, and your body makes most of what it needs, then takes the rest from the skin or bones of meat or fish. A third of the frame that holds you up is made of it, skin or bone, and in the cord of your back it is the signal that tells a nerve to stop firing.

This will is a chemistry, one you share with your kin, a family in your body whose path is not wasting strength. What that family releases is everything your body still holds against itself, until every part of you works as it was made to. That is the rest this energy ends in: not a mood, your body letting go of everything it held.

keywords: Every Wish a Wish for Home

fields.essence: The pressure toward what has not happened yet is this energy, the hunger in you for a better life than the one you are standing in. It pictures more than is here and wants to feel it. It is the first move of every new stretch in a life, the wanting that comes before there is anything to want, and you feel it low in the body, the way hunger is felt. It is older than you: everything that came before you presses in it, dragging you down and urging you to break free in the same moment.
fields.glance:
The pressure toward what has not happened yet is this energy, the hunger in you for a better life than the one you are standing in. It pictures more than is here and wants to feel it. It is the first move of every new stretch in a life, the wanting that comes before there is anything to want, and you feel it low in the body, the way hunger is felt. It is older than you: everything that came before you presses in it, dragging you down and urging you to break free in the same moment.

The hunger read right is a way of seeing rather than a way of leaving. You feel what is on its way before it arrives, and you set to work bringing it through. Whatever you have pictured is held lightly, the way you hold a plan for a trip, since the road will change it and you would rather have the road. Small plans are good, what to eat tomorrow, where to meet a friend; it is the large plan, the whole life arranged in the head, that this hunger is forever tempted into. The ones who carry this best live simply, less attached to how their own story turns out, and are glad to be in it.

This energy comes in cycles. A dream rises, gives you years of hope and falls away, then another rises in its place. The hope is so good that you can live on it without ever setting out, and whole industries are built to keep you there. Every wish carries an if, if this came I would be happy, and life takes the ifs away one at a time. It never feels like a kindness, though it is one. What goes each time is the picture; the wanting under it stays, and it was always the same wanting. Each turn is another chance to read it right. Begin this time, with the nearest thing, and let the story find its own ending.
fields.iching:
You are in a time of having less, and the whole question is whether you choose it. Loss is coming either way. Taken from you, it is only loss; given up on purpose, from below to feed what stands above you, it becomes an offering, and an offering is how a hard time turns into a good one. What you give does not have to be much. Two small bowls carried to the altar are enough when what is in them is sincere, because a small thing given honestly reaches further than a large thing given for show.

What it asks of you is to decrease yourself first. Curb your anger, hold back the appetites that run ahead of you, bring whatever is in excess back to its right size. It is heavy at the start and light afterward, which is the order this time keeps, so do not read the heaviness as a sign that you are wrong. Keep harm at a distance while you are lighter than usual. Do not dwell on what has concluded, and set out on what is next, because this is a time when moving on goes well. The turn is already in it: where decrease ends, increase begins, and what you gave from the bottom comes back from the top.

In the body this is the hand. Notice what yours is holding now, and how tightly. An offering begins as a closed hand opening. Hold yourself the way the mountain holds the lake, still above, giving below, with nothing in it grasped. Mountain over Lake: the still height, and at its foot the open water. The lake gives up its water as mist, the mist feeds the heights, and so the low is lessened to fill the high. The old character shows a hand and a ceremonial vessel, an offering carried to the altar: to decrease is to give up what is yours on purpose. Decrease
fields.gene_keys:
Fantasy Anticipation Emanation The same dream, once you have seen to the bottom of it, becomes a way of sensing what is coming. Under every fantasy you have ever had, the lover or the fortune, there is one ache, to connect, to be part of something whole. Once you know what the picture was really asking for, the picture can be used. You stop mistaking a wish for a sign. You begin to feel the shape of a future that is actually forming, the way a musician hears a whole piece before it is written and simply takes it down. The dreamer and the one who brings it through have the same dream; one is working while the other is still looking.

The light thrown down the road is walked toward now, and the road corrects the picture as you go. Because you traced your own dreams to the root, you can see where another person's dream is really heading, and sense the moment a stuck pattern in them is ready to break, a help advice never is. Two things last, children and stories. This energy knows how a story goes; it knows the ending and can wait for it. A dream of a better life sits in you, and most days you live in the dream instead of the life. The pressure that made it was the pressure to grow; through a tired mind it comes out as the pressure to feel happy, and the mind paints a picture, the right person or the money. Then it falls in love with the picture. You hold the key to the dream and never turn it in the lock, because what you live on is not the dream coming true but the hope it gives. Hope is cheaper than a first step. The gauge in you swings. Empty, you dream of being full. Full, you feel the weight of everything behind you and want to be rid of it.

The picture was a light thrown down the road to show the way, and you have stood still, looking at the light. Every dream you have will be taken from you, one at a time, which is good news that never arrives dressed as one. When one goes, look at what is left. The emptiness can be filled, though never by the next picture, and never by anything you achieve. You thought you were travelling forward, and you were going back. Every dream you had was an impulse from the source you came from, looking for the way home the only way it knew, throwing little lights ahead; followed all the way, the lights lead back to where they were thrown from. Here the picture is gone, the road with it, and no one is left standing. It is not brought on by anything you do. It arrives from nowhere, and the one it has happened to cannot say how, since no one remains for it to have happened to.

There is no more hunger, so no more pressure to become anything. Speak, and people hear an agenda in it; keep still, they hear one in that. You are caught, and it does not matter. All you are is the beginning of the story and its end. It was a dream, and you had to be asleep to hear it.
fields.human_design:
Imagination The pressure to picture more than is here, then go and feel it, is this energy in the body. Gate 41 is the door it comes through: the drive to imagine a fuller life, a better world, and then to want it with the whole body. It is the first pressure in every new stretch of experience, the one that opens the year, and what it starts it does not always finish, since starting is its work. From outside it can look like restlessness, someone never satisfied with the room they are in. What is going on is simpler: the imagination is doing what it was built to do, refusing to call the present the whole story.

The cost is being taken for a dreamer. People carrying this hear that their ideas are unrealistic, or too much, and learn to keep the picture to themselves, until the picture curdles into the worst that could happen instead of the best. People who carry this all their lives learn to share the picture when the time is right, not before, and to rest in the pleasure of imagining, which was the point all along.
fields.tarot: This code stands alone in the Ring of Origin. It is the only card in the deck with no siblings in its ring, because the chemistry it carries, the start codon, is coded by this one place and nowhere else. Every other ring is a family. This one is a single point, the source the other families thread back to. It is the beginning the whole cycle empties toward and pours out from. A figure kneels at the water's edge and tips her jug back into the pool, and the Arcana of this card arrive along three separate routes. The ring gives one Major, The Fool, the zero that opens the deck and closes it, beginning and end in a single figure. The two trigrams give their own faces: Mountain above as the Hierophant and the Hermit, the keeper of tradition and the seeker who climbs alone; Lake below as the Lovers and the Star, the choice that unites and the hope that pours itself out. The Fool steps off the edge, and the trigrams answer him, stillness above that receives, water below that gives itself away.
fields.body:
In you this energy is given to the adrenals, and the reason is the morning. Two small glands sit one on top of each of your kidneys, high at the back under the last ribs, and they run the day's tide. The tide is lowest around midnight, rises through the last hours of your sleep, and is highest in the hour after you wake, so the day starts in you before you do. Before your eyes open the glands have readied you, whether the day will be good or not. That is this energy's work too, beginning ahead of you, and the adrenals are where the body does the same.

You cannot feel them; a hand laid flat on your back below the ribs covers a kidney with its cap and finds neither. Their work you can feel. When you know the hour you must be up, the tide rises earlier to meet it, and most people have woken just before the alarm with no idea why. That was the part of you that starts the day, starting it. The hunger for what has not come has a chemistry in you, and the substance is methionine. Every protein your body makes begins with this one piece, because the way the code spells it is also the way the code says begin. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from eggs, fish or meat, and beans are short of it. Once the building is under way the first piece is most often trimmed off, and the finished thing goes without it.

So every story your body tells opens on the same word, the capital letter at the head of every sentence in you. Beans on your plate are short of this, rice is short of another; together they are short of nothing, which is why every old kitchen arrived at rice and beans. The first piece of everything built in you tonight came from a plate.

fields.essence: Increase is the energy here, more poured into you than you were holding, until the level rises and runs over toward whatever stands lower than you. It comes from outside, the way a good year comes to a field, and it has a second half that is easy to miss: it goes on coming only while it is passed on. It is also the part of you that knows how a thing wants to end, so that what is finished can be set down to make room.
fields.glance:
Increase is the energy here, more poured into you than you were holding, until the level rises and runs over toward whatever stands lower than you. It comes from outside, the way a good year comes to a field, and it has a second half that is easy to miss: it goes on coming only while it is passed on. It is also the part of you that knows how a thing wants to end, so that what is finished can be set down to make room.

Increase that is passed on as it comes trusts the shape of a life more than the plan for it. Hope is the growing force in you, the wish that things be better than they are; it turns into disappointment only when the mind takes hold of it and sets a date on what must arrive. Let the date go and keep the hope. Give as you gain, without waiting until you have enough, because the giving is what keeps the level rising. What you seek for yourself is on the right road when it turns out to be good for everyone near you as well.

The way through is to let things end. Every seven years or so you are standing in a body most of which has been replaced, cell by cell, without your noticing; something in you had to die each time for the new to have a place, and a life closes its cycles the same way. There will be a stretch when you catch yourself waiting for things to come right before the real living starts, and the real living is the waiting. See through that once, all the way down, and what you were saving for later is here, ready to be finished.
fields.iching:
More is coming in than you were holding, and it is coming from above you, from the one with more than enough loosening their grip so that the level downstream rises. That is the shape of this time: what is full pours toward what is empty, and for once you are on the empty side. It was not asked for and it cannot be refused. It is a season, and a season does not stay; the time to undertake the large thing is now, while the water is high enough to cross.

What it asks is that the gain keep moving. Wind and thunder feed each other: the thunder shakes something loose, the wind carries it across the field; what one starts the other spreads. So the instruction is small and daily. When you see something good in another, move toward it, as quickly as wind moves. When you find a fault in yourself, mend it, with the nerve thunder has. Kept for yourself, the increase stops, and what stops is set upon from every side. Passed on, it goes on coming.

In the body this energy is the legs: the feet that take the first step, and the thighs that carry the rest of you after them. Notice where you are held now, whether you are sitting on what has come or already standing. Stand, let the weight settle into the thighs, and take the crossing while the water carries you. Wind over Thunder: the shock that starts things below, and above it the wind that carries what was started across the whole field. The upper sign is the tree as much as the wind, so wood grows here too. The old character is water poured into a vessel until it brims and runs over; the word means to add, to enrich, more than enough. Increase
fields.gene_keys:
Expectation Detachment Celebration Detachment means feeling more, not less. The word sounds like arms folded at a distance from your own life; the thing itself is the reverse, because you have stopped letting an expectation clamp down on what happens before it can land, and you can even enjoy being disappointed. It cannot be forced. Hold a feeling down by discipline and the attachment thickens, which is how the strictest fall hardest; the real thing comes by yielding, letting every feeling rise all the way, not always acted on, never refused.

From there your life reads like a story. You are inside it, writing it as you go, and you are its reader too, absorbed, turning the pages, never lost in the words. Let go of each expectation as quickly as life overturns it, or the waters of regret close over your head. You can see the places where you still want to steer, and you can let the plot change. What looks like distance is trust in life deep enough to stop bracing, and it is found by giving in to your own ordinary humanity, breathing the air, not flinching from what hurts. Nearly everyone is waiting for the part of the story where it comes right. The money sorted, the love in place, room at last to breathe, but first a few things to clear up; so the living is put off, and put off, until the years have gone. Hope is not the trouble. Hope is the growing force in you, the wish that things be better than they are; it stays clean until the mind takes hold of it, giving it a date and a shape. Then whatever arrives is measured against the shape, falls short, and the disappointment becomes a way of seeing.

Underneath sits the one expectation nobody escapes, the ending of the body, written into every cell you have. The unease you feel about time running out comes from there. Bright or grim, an expectation narrows your eyes to the one outcome you are braced for, so that the good in front of you goes unseen and what this moment could hold is closed down. It is never too late to be in the now; it takes seeing through what you were waiting for, once, with nothing held back. The story ends here, and what is left is laughter. Being detached still kept a seam between the watcher and the watched; now the watcher has become the watched, so only one thing is happening. Everything is still felt as dying, every cell in you dying from the moment it was made, so that you were never a thing so much as a passage, matter turning to energy on its way through. Somewhere below thought, something gets the joke. The whole serious quest was the set-up, and you laugh because you let yourself be tricked.

Sit by a river following the currents with your eyes, then stop following and look through them: the river loses its direction, coming at you from everywhere at once. Birth and death stop being two events. Nothing brings this on, no practice earns it, so there is nothing left to do but celebrate, and whoever it has happened to wants only to share the laugh.
fields.human_design:
Growth Carrying a thing to its close is the pressure here. Gate 42 is where it enters: the drive to see a cycle through, to stay with a piece of work, or with someone, until it has ripened, and then to know the hour it is done. It is the pull that feels a loose end as a weight on the room, the appetite for the harvest rather than the planting. Time is on its side; a thing that needs years is given its years.

From outside it looks like patience, or stubbornness. The cost runs two ways. Held past the end, it clings to what is over because finishing was the whole point, and forgets that some growth is knowing when to let go. Turned into a demand to start everything as well, it fills a life with half-done things and a quiet judgement about them, or it rushes a close to be rid of the weight before the thing was ready.
