As the pressure falls away, the life in you runs clearer. Bliss itself, when it comes, is made in you, a release of chemicals in the brain, felt as gladness with no cause.

fields.essence: The reach toward another person is this energy, the drive in you to get through whatever stands between you and be known on the far side of it. In you it is felt first as a wariness. Alone in a room you are at ease; someone walks in, and a faint guardedness starts up in the air between you, so old that you stopped noticing it. The reach and the wariness are one thing. What you keep hidden is what the other has to fear, and it is the fear that holds the two of you apart.
fields.glance:
The reach toward another person is this energy, the drive in you to get through whatever stands between you and be known on the far side of it. In you it is felt first as a wariness. Alone in a room you are at ease; someone walks in, and a faint guardedness starts up in the air between you, so old that you stopped noticing it. The reach and the wariness are one thing. What you keep hidden is what the other has to fear, and it is the fear that holds the two of you apart.

A life where this goes right begins with honesty, and the honesty begins at home. Before you can be honest with another heart you have to be honest with your own, about what you are hiding and why; most of what you find there is old pain rather than anything shameful. Held instead of run from, the pain lets go, and when it does there is room around your heart that was not there before. That room is what closeness is. It is not something you do to another person; it is what shows once you no longer need them to be different, and someone who feels that from you is free to be honest in turn.

The way is not to run from it. Every time the guardedness is blamed on the other person, the same knot ties itself again somewhere else, because it was never out there. Turn back toward the wariness, into the body, where it lives. Whatever you meet there is yours, and the moment you own it there is nothing left in you for anyone to fear.
fields.iching:
Something between you and other people has set hard; this is its breaking up. A suspicion gone solid, a self held so tight it has shut everyone out: the wind is on it now, and what was rigid begins to move. It feels like loss while it happens. It is a thaw. What it asks of you is warmth first. A cold wind chills the pool to ice; a warm one melts it, and what you scatter carries your own temperature, so if you go out cold, cold is what you spread. Warm yourself first, since no warmth comes in from outside to do it for you.

The old picture is the king going to the temple. When his people have drifted apart, hard with suspicion, he does not drive them back together. He stands in the ancestral hall with his whole heart, and the scattered gather on their own, because sincerity draws what force scatters. Scatter what ought to be scattered, the faction, the held grudge, and what ought not to be scattered can gather again. Now is the time for the big crossing: a boat on the wide water with the wind behind it, pushed forward by the same thing that broke up the ice.

In the body this energy is the thighs, the part of you that carries you across a room toward someone, or out of it. Notice which way yours are turned now. Stand easy in them, ready to cross, and let the warmth go first. Wind over Water: a wind crossing a pool, the still surface going to ripples and spray. What had frozen is melting, what had set hard is coming apart, the way fog lifts off a field or a crowd breaks up and goes home. The old name means to scatter; it is said of clouds, of suspicions, of a fear that had settled in and now lifts. Dispersion
fields.gene_keys:
Dishonesty Intimacy Transparency Intimacy begins by allowing the fear to exist. Admit that it is there between you, understand it, let it stay, and the allowing works like a valve: the whole force behind it comes through. It is not gentle. This is the raw power that makes new life, creative and destructive at once; what it destroys is the pattern that kept two people separate. Allowed all the way in, it opens you to a state above the one you were living in.

Two people met like this make a third thing between them, a field neither had alone, and the more unlike the two are, the further it can take them. What dawns in it is not in the belly, where the force started; it rises to the heart, and there two people meet inside one awareness. The nearest thing to it you may already know is falling in love, when you feel inside the other and feel them from far away. It is honesty balanced with kindness. You do not pour everything out; your heart decides how much to share, and it listens as much as it speaks. Dishonesty here is not a lie you tell. It is the part of you kept back from everyone, so old that it came with you. The fear it guards is not in you but in the air between two people; alone, it is not there. That fear is also the pull: as long as something in you stays hidden there is something for the other to be wary of, and the wariness draws them, which is why the moment you stop being afraid of a person the pull goes slack. None of this was chosen. It is the source of every hidden agenda you have ever had.

What it costs is the world made lonely: rooms full of people, and almost nobody known. The dishonesty begins inward, in the story you tell yourself about why you did what you did, and the story always moves the blame outside you. Then you change the person, or the country, and the knot ties itself again, because it was never out there. Under it is old pain, stacked in the body, most of it handed down to you, and any part of you that does not own that pain is the dishonest part. Transparency is what remains when nothing in you is left to hide, because there is no separate one left to hide it. What was a self has gone back into the sea it came from. What stays is a clear mirror: life passes through it and it adds no comment, no judgement, none of the story you lay over what you see. Inside and outside were the last wall; when that goes, everything is within you.

From here everyone alive is your brother or your sister, and no one is an island. Two joined like this cannot be parted by distance, or by death. Fear turns out to have been a skin, and this is the far side of it. The one purpose this energy ever had was to break down every barrier to union, and when the last one is down it is no longer needed.
fields.human_design:
Sexuality The force that gets through to another person is this energy's pressure in the body. Gate 59 is where it enters: the drive to break the barrier between you and someone else, making closeness where there was none. At its root it is the drive to make new life, the force that carries a species on, and it is impersonal, choosing for you whom you are drawn to. Above that root it reaches for people, wanting to understand them and be understood, taking down the walls between them almost without trying.

The trouble built in is where and with whom. The same force that fills a house with children starts wars when nobody asked it first. From outside it looks like someone who cannot leave a boundary alone, or who uses closeness to get their way; what is going on is a reach that has not yet learned to wait to be met. People who carry this all their lives learn to be clear before they act, and that the same power that takes a wall down can be used to take a person, which is the one use of it that leaves you alone in the end.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Union, this code is the master key. Its siblings, UL 4, 7, and 29, carry the rest of the path home: forgiveness, the virtue it uncovers, and the devotion that pours the self out into others. Together they are the family that has governed human relationship and its breakdown, and their whole aim is to bring people into one body. Ring and trigrams both bring Tarot faces to this card. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Lovers, the covenant. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Wind above as the Wheel of Fortune and Death, the turning point and the shapeshifting; Water below as the High Priestess, who perceives what has not yet spoken. The Lovers, the Wheel, Death and the High Priestess tell a single story, a union that turns on a threshold and reads the depth before it crosses.
fields.body:
Your reach for another body is given to the sacral plexus with the organs it serves, and the reason is that this is where new life is made. Against the inner face of the bone at the base of your spine a weave of nerves gathers; out of it run the nerves to everything between your legs, carrying the feeling of the place and readying your body for another body without a thought from you. In the same low ground are the ovaries or the testes, the part of you that carries you on into someone who does not exist yet, and the old physicians stored in the same low ground what makes children.

Each person you have ever met is here because this place in two other people did its work, and so are you. This place is also the part of you least under your instruction: nothing in you here waits for your permission, and nothing here can be talked into readiness by the head. That is the part of you this energy is given to. The longing for another has a substance in you, and the substance is valine. Your body does not make it; it comes in with what you eat, more of it in a bowl of oats than in white rice, and when food is short your body can burn it as sugar. Three other things in you share it, and it is the same substance in all four. Between you and someone you love there is a chemistry that does its work in silence; this is part of what it is made of.

The substance runs the whole way through you: the forgiving of yourself, the goodness that shows once you have, the pouring of yourself out into others, then this, the last of the four, where the pouring has emptied you and there is no longer an inside to keep anything in.

fields.essence: Limits are this energy, the line drawn so that what moves through you can take a shape. A river with no banks is a flood that goes nowhere; with banks it is a river, and it arrives. In you it is the part that says this far, this much, no further, so that a piece of work or a whole life can stand up and be something. It is not a brake. It is what lets force go somewhere.
fields.glance:
Limits are this energy, the line drawn so that what moves through you can take a shape. A river with no banks is a flood that goes nowhere; with banks it is a river, and it arrives. In you it is the part that says this far, this much, no further, so that a piece of work or a whole life can stand up and be something. It is not a brake. It is what lets force go somewhere.

A good line is a balance between two pulls. There is a force in you that wants to rise, reach, fly, and a force that pulls back down, tightens, settles for less. You live between them, and neither is meant to win: too much of the first burns you, too much of the second shrivels you. You need the structures, and you need to be free of them at the same time. The one who carries this well builds a frame without living in it. Without a limit nothing in you has a shape, and without a shape you cannot say what you want; the discipline that draws the line is how you find out.

The low of it is a frame kept past its season. You built a way of thinking once, about money or about the person you live with. After long enough the walls stopped being something you made and became the edge of the world. This force does not yield to being pushed. It waits for one thing, which is time, because everything alive moves in cycles and rights itself when it is let. When a frame has done its work, let it crack, and keep what it was built to hold.
fields.iching:
What you are in asks for a limit, and the limit is what will let it succeed. A lake stays a lake by holding a measured amount of water. Too little and it dries. Too much and it breaks its banks. So the level is watched, and the watching never ends. A cane of bamboo grows tall because it is jointed, each knot a small stop that lets the next length begin. What you are building will stand the same way, by the places where you say this far.

What it asks of you is to make the measures: to reckon what you will spend, how far you will go, what you will not do, then to weigh your own conduct against them. A measure made well injures nothing you own and harms no one near you. Heaven and earth keep to theirs, which is why there are four seasons rather than one long day.

There is one warning, and it is the centre of the matter. A limit that has gone bitter must not be carried on. A rule kept past its season, severe and hard to bear, stops serving the thing it was made for; the harder you hold it, the sooner its road runs out. The measure has to be measured too. In the body this is the joints, the knee and the knuckle, a limit that is the whole reason a limb can bend. Feel yours now, whether they are easy or locked. A joint held stiff does not make you stronger, only unable to move. Water over Lake: the stream, and under it the lake that holds it. The old character is the joint in a stalk of bamboo, the knot that divides the cane into lengths, the reason it stands so tall without snapping: a division that makes the parts and joins them at once. Above, the stream keeps coming; below, the lake takes a measured amount and no more. Limitation
fields.gene_keys:
Limitation Realism Justice Knowing how things get made is what this energy becomes: what the world of form allows and what it does not, which is why people who have it are so sought after. An idea, however good, will not enter the world on its own. It needs a shell, as a seed does, or it never takes. So you build the shell, or you graft the new shoot onto the old root, bringing change through what already stands rather than against it. You hold the structure lightly, with something like a smile, knowing it is a means, not the point, since every structure is doomed. That is realism. It has a natural business sense, building the kind of frame that bends when the ground moves.

Then it waits. Nothing new arrives on schedule; it comes in the gap between what you meant and what you built, once the easel is up, on a day you did not choose. There are stretches when nothing moves, arriving as suddenly as they leave, and you do not interfere. The highest part of this is knowing when to stand back and let the frame go. Frozen patterns are the low of this energy: life closing into tighter shapes over the years, until the openings that once let something in have shut. It is the counterweight to being alive, and it works through the mind, which likes to build. Thought goes round the same track it went round yesterday, about the bank account, about the government, and nothing original gets in, because the door was never left ajar. Out in the world it is red tape, the law so tangled it no longer protects anyone, the child made to sit at a desk at the age when the whole body wants to run. It cannot stand the new, and it cannot stand the young.

What it costs you is trust. Life has a way of righting itself, in its own time. This is the part of you that cannot believe that, so it holds everything still and calls the stillness safety. Push it and it does not move; it waits for one thing only, which is time. Nothing you build will last, the body included. Knowing that is the first loosening of the grip. Justice is what this energy becomes, and it is not the word as it is used. Not punishment, not reward, not a scale weighing a deed. A man once stole the silver of the one house that had taken him in, was caught, and was brought back to its door. The owner told the police the silver had been given to him, and that undid the thief further than any sentence could. Being forgiven cracks you open. From here nobody is punished, because no separate person is left to have done the thing; the balance rights itself with no one keeping the books.

What loosens at this height are the laws themselves, time first, then the pull that holds matter together. What that feels like is weight leaving. Drop the past and you are light, in both senses of the word. Every wall you ever built turns out to have been holding you up only until you could stand.
fields.human_design: Conservation Gate 60 is the pressure to bring something new into form, within limits, and its name here is Conservation: keep what still works. Out of everything that arrives, most of it noise, it feels for the one thing worth carrying forward and holds it until it has a shape. From outside that looks like a brake, a refusal to move; what is happening is a flower coming up out of mud, which cannot be hurried and cannot be skipped. In a time of loss the same pressure keeps you looking at what is still standing rather than at what has fallen, which is what lets a person rebuild. Its cost is intense. The pressure to produce a result is there before the result is. When nothing shows you can go low and believe something is wrong with you, when the timing is simply not yet. People who carry this all their lives learn a particular patience: the seed under the ground is growing while nothing is visible, and there is nothing anyone can do to push it.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Gaia, this code stands as the body of the earth made dense, structure itself given form. Its two siblings, UL 19 and UL 61, carry the rest: the sensitivity that feels across all living things, and the inner truth hidden at the core of every particle. Together they hold the planet's own chemistry, the awareness that moves between every form of life. A card called Limitation draws the Empress, of all the Majors, and draws nothing else. The Empress is the one Major the Ring of Gaia carries, and she is the right face for it: the earth mother, abundance held in a body, fertility that needs a form to pour through. The two trigram axes are not carried here. Neither Water nor Lake keys to a Major in the source, so neither is invented to fill the gap.
fields.body:
In the body this energy is given to the colon, and the reason is the banks. A litre and a half of liquid comes into it every day, the leftover of the gut above. All but a cupful of the water goes back into your blood, so what arrived as a flood leaves with a shape. It holds what it has for a day or two, then moves, a few long pushes a day, most often after the first meal, since a filling stomach sets the far end going. Nothing you decide changes that, except at the very end, where one muscle, the only one along the gut, waits for you. Felt from inside, the shape comes from what is taken back, the hold has its own time, and the last word is yours.

Lie on your back and press in low on the left. Sometimes a firm rope is there under your fingers, the last bend, felt only when it is full. You are pressing on the part of you that gives the day's leftover its shape. The frame your body keeps has a chemistry in it, and one of its substances is isoleucine. You cannot make it; your body takes it in, from meat, cheese or beans, or goes without. Three energies in you share this one substance; here it is at its heaviest, the plain material density of the earth, held as you are between an upward drive and the pull back down.

In you it is taken apart in the muscle you move with, the part of you that works against the pull of the ground, where most of its kind are sent to the liver instead. The same substance is in the moment a thought breaks out of its habit, so what holds you and what frees you are one chemistry in you.

fields.essence: Inner truth is the energy here, the knowing in you that has no proof, and it comes with a question. Why is the first question anyone asks, and in you it never stops: it wells up from somewhere deeper than thought, refusing every made-up answer. It is what you know without knowing how you know, the thing you would still hold to if everyone at the table disagreed. In a life it is the wondering that keeps you awake, with a quiet certainty underneath it.
fields.glance:
Inner truth is the energy here, the knowing in you that has no proof, and it comes with a question. Why is the first question anyone asks, and in you it never stops: it wells up from somewhere deeper than thought, refusing every made-up answer. It is what you know without knowing how you know, the thing you would still hold to if everyone at the table disagreed. In a life it is the wondering that keeps you awake, with a quiet certainty underneath it.

This knowing stops needing the question answered once you trust it. The why cannot be answered by thinking, because thought goes round in a circle to the question again, and a mind under that pressure will accept anything that promises to end it. What comes instead is inspiration, in flashes, when it comes and for as long as it stays; after one you are never quite the same. It cannot be forced, so it has to be waited for, and between the flashes there are flat days. The way through them is making something with your hands, a garden or a song. The moment the making begins the mind empties, and what was troubling it settles like silt in still water.

Stand inside the question instead of running from it. Not knowing is the whole of what is asked; the mind is not your enemy, only it was never there to keep you safe. Something in you is sure without a reason, the way you know a friend is telling the truth before the sentence is finished, and that sureness moves people more than any argument could. Live without the answer long enough and the pressure of the question turns into wonder.
fields.iching:
Sincerity is asked of you here, and it is a thing you are, not a thing you say. Truth held in the middle of you reaches people the way wind reaches water, unseen, plainly shown in what it moves. It reaches even those nobody else can reach, the ones who trust no one and have heard every argument. What moves them is not a better case. It is that there is no gap in you between what you show and what you hold.

What it asks is emptiness in the middle. Go in with no fixed idea of how it should come out, the way an empty boat crosses water that a loaded one would sink in, and you can cross what looks too wide. Where you have to judge someone, judge slowly: take the time to understand why they did what they did before you decide what it costs them, and put the sentence off as long as you can. Answer, rather than react. Stay firm in what you know without being able to prove it, because that is where this strength is made.

In the body this energy is the thighs above the mouth: what carries you, over what you say. Notice whether the two agree now, whether your walk and your word are one thing. Let the chest open, the middle of you empty, and speak only what the whole of you is standing on. Wind over Lake: the wind cannot be seen, and the water shows it, every gust written on the surface. What is inside you is like that, unseen, known only by what it moves. The traditional character is an arrow through the centre of a target, beside a bird's foot laid over its young: a bird sitting on the nest, truth kept warm in the middle until its day comes. Inner Truth
fields.gene_keys:
Psychosis Inspiration Sanctity Inspiration is breath coming in, and this energy at its fullest is exactly that: something enters you that you did not think, changing the way you see. It comes in flashes, sudden and short, sometimes a longer spell; after even one you are not the person you were. Each flash takes apart a piece of what the mind had built in place of reality, and the energy that was tied up in the building is let loose, wanting to be made into something. So this is a maker's energy. When the mind is troubled, take up a trowel or a pencil; the moment the making starts the mind lets go, empties, and leaves only what matters, along with the thing you made.

It cannot be forced, so patience is most of the work, and the days in between can be flat. A man who lost his wife rose every dawn for a year to pour the grief into a garden; at the end there was a garden, a clear mind, something made for her. Being born in a body is being born with a wound, and this is how the wound is tended. Losing touch with what is real is the ordinary state of a mind, and in this energy it shows first as a question, the question why. It is the first word anyone learns to ask, and in you it rises from somewhere under thought, as a pressure the mind cannot bear to leave open. So the mind answers it, with anything, a religion or a science, whatever promises to make the pressure stop. The mind is sick for one reason: it is trying to find itself with itself, and it cannot, any more than an eye can see itself. The worst of it is worship. The moment you put someone above you as the one who knows, you have set yourself below the truth in you, and there you stay.

Everyone is in this to some degree, and being in it is no fault. What is asked is not that you think harder. The only release is to walk into the middle of the pressure instead of making it go away, and that takes apart what the mind built, which is why it has to be done slowly, in a body, on the ground. Holiness is what is left when the inspiration has used itself up. One day a great silence comes down, full and heavy; the mind stops, all of it, in the middle of a question. The pressure that drove the question leaves the head to go out through the whole of you, everywhere at once, so that you are entirely empty and endlessly full in one moment, with no one inside to have the experience. The question why does not get answered here; it ends. What remains is living without answers, being the mystery instead of solving it, knowing nothing, in its own time. Until you rest in this you are asleep, whatever else you know. It is a lonely way, a lovely one: a flash of it, then a fall and the work begun again, until the night you sit on open rock while the full moon drifts up the mountain, with nothing left to empty.
fields.human_design:
Wonder Wonder is the drive here, the pressure to know why. Gate 61 is where it enters: the part of you that reaches past what can be explained toward the mystery of the thing itself, and comes back with a knowing it cannot account for. You know things. You do not know how you know, you could not show your working, and you know them all the same. It is the drive that sits up at night with a question nobody else in the house is asking.

From outside it looks like being lost in thought, or out of step; people carrying this are often misunderstood, and the cost is that they begin to doubt what they know because nobody around them can confirm it. The other cost is the pressure itself. Left to run, the need to figure it out turns bitter, and the story of why things happened to you replaces the wonder that they happened at all. People who carry it all their lives learn the one trade this drive offers: give up needing the answer and keep the wonder, since being present turns out to hold more than knowing ever did.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of Gaia, this code is the inner question of the living planet itself. Its two siblings, UL 19 and UL 60, carry the rest of the family: the drawing near, and the limit that holds. Together they say that evolution is a force breaking out from inside matter, that the whole blue-green world is working toward its own inner truth, and that to find it you look inward. Two of the three Tarot axes carry cards here, and the third is left open. The codon ring gives one Arcana, the Empress, the fertile ground that holds and nourishes. The Wind above gives two faces, the Wheel of Fortune and Death, the turning and the shedding. The Lake below carries no keyed Major in the source. An Empress carried on the Wheel and through Death is a nurturing depth that turns and dies and turns again, the mystery composting itself into new form.
fields.body:
In the middle of your head, where the two halves of the brain meet, is a gland the size of a grain of rice called the pineal gland, and this energy is given to it because it works in the dark. Nearly everything in your brain comes in pairs, left and right; this one is single, in the centre. It never sees light; it learns from your eyes whether the day has gone, and while the light is on it does nothing at all. When the light has gone it begins, and what it makes is your body's dark. The question in you rises the same way, from a part of the mind no light reaches, and the knowing comes without your seeing how it was made.

Feel it over an evening. Sit in a dim room; over an hour or two your body slows and grows heavy, which is the gland at its work. Turn a bright light on and within minutes it stops. It cannot be felt happening, only arriving, as everything from this part of you arrives. The pressure of the mystery in you has a substance, and the substance is isoleucine. It is one of the twenty small pieces every protein in you is built from, one of the nine your body cannot make; it comes in with meat or beans, or not at all. It is the twin of another of the twenty, the same atoms in a slightly different order: two things that weigh the same, spelled from the same pieces, are not the same thing, and the difference is inside, out of your sight.

The mystery beats in every cell of your body, and whatever is of true value in you is hidden inside your body, never on the outside. That is chemistry as much as feeling, one substance shared with your kin. Taken apart in you, it goes two ways, part burned and part turned to sugar, which its twin cannot do.

keywords: Naming Things Instead of Feeling Them

fields.essence: Exactness is this energy, the right word in the right place and the small thing done well. In you it is the pause before you speak, when you feel what a word weighs, and the eye that catches the detail everyone else walked past. It lives in the quiet work most people never notice: the sentence cut to what it means, or the one small thing put right before anyone asked. Where others fill a silence, you wait, then say the one thing, and people lean in without knowing why.
fields.glance:
Exactness is this energy, the right word in the right place and the small thing done well. In you it is the pause before you speak, when you feel what a word weighs, and the eye that catches the detail everyone else walked past. It lives in the quiet work most people never notice: the sentence cut to what it means, or the one small thing put right before anyone asked. Where others fill a silence, you wait, then say the one thing, and people lean in without knowing why.

Exactness in its right place is warm, because the heart is choosing and the mind is only finding the words. Cleverness is of the head, where it can be argued with; understanding is of the heart, which a person with no schooling at all can have whole. So you spend words carefully, and what you say is spare enough to land. The truer it gets, the fewer words it needs, since the true ones keep dissolving back into silence. A touch is enough. A touch set in the right place is what turns a wheel.

Leave things out. There are days when the details are where you hide, the list growing so that the feeling underneath is never reached, and the fussing then is fear in the clothes of care. Put the small thing right, then stop. Wait until the word is the one, then let it go alone, with room around it, because the room is what lets it land. A crossing made by a small margin is still a crossing.
fields.iching:
You are in a season of small things, and the small things are the whole of what can be done now. The stir in you wants to go up, to make the large move, and the ground you stand on swallows most of the sound: what carries is what stays near. The old text gives its counsel to a bird. A bird that keeps climbing finds nothing to land on, while the one that comes down has a branch, so the message the bird leaves behind it is this: not up, down. Great good fortune lies that way.

What it asks is that you go a little past the mark in the small things, on the side of humility. Be a little more respectful than the occasion needs, grieve a little longer than is expected, spend a little less, since in a time like this too little is safer than too much. Do the near thing a little better than anyone else would, and go up one rung at a time. Do not reach for the great thing; it is not the hour, and reaching for it is how the year is lost. Strive downward, and let the downward striving lift you.

In the body this energy is the feet, the part of you that wants to go, held here by the hands, the part of you that keeps things where they are. Notice where you are holding yourself now. Keep the hands busy with the near thing, and let the feet stay on the ground. Thunder over Mountain: the sound that shakes the sky, going off above a peak that swallows it, so that it carries only a little way. The figure is a bird, its body the two firm lines in the middle, its wings the soft lines above and below. The traditional character shows a house with more on its beam than the beam was built for: going a little past the mark. Small Preponderance
fields.gene_keys:
Intellect Precision Impeccability Precision is the heart in charge with the mind in its service, and it is warmer than the word sounds. It begins the day the questioning turns round on itself: the one lost in details starts to wonder why, and the one who used facts as a weapon finds that the misery was self-made, from years of looking at anything but their own pain. Then the windows are clean. You look at the tree, take it in, its aliveness, before you reach for its name, and the name comes out right because it came second.

This exactness is not stiffness. It is knowing which pattern is true and which only looks it, then putting people where they belong to each other, the way the seasons are exact without a clock. Sometimes the order has to go through disorder to arrive, and you can move through both without losing your footing. People cannot help listening when the heart is doing the arranging. The fear that comes with it, of being laughed at for speaking from the heart, is the sign that you are. Knowing the name of a thing is where this energy goes wrong, because a name is not the thing. Look at a tree through the clever mind and you see what you were taught, its name, its kind, never the tree. That mind lives on facts, and a fact cannot exist without a name, so a life built from facts is a life built out of words, on sand. Today's facts are tomorrow's fables. Your days run on numbers, the bank, the phone, and it is hard to see how much of what you take for the world is only a thing said about it.

You were not born like this. A child is already intelligent, in the way it moves its arms, in the brightness of its eyes, and school put information in until the brightness went quiet. Intelligence is of the heart, cleverness of the head, and the head will argue to the end rather than give itself up. Nobody is home, and what is done from here cannot be wrong. The words no longer come through the mind at all; they come up out of the silence, plain, and there are fewer of them the higher you go, because they keep dissolving back into it. What has influence now is not what you make but the moment you make it in, the presence behind the act. A song never heard by anyone is not lost; the making of it stays, and it is the only thing that does.

Nothing in you is out of place, even the broken parts. A bowl mended with gold in the cracks is worth more than the one that never broke, and you are that bowl. Fear is gone, which is only to say there is no one left to be afraid, and the woodpecker, that small bird with the bright throat, goes on finding its food in the dead tree.
fields.human_design:
Preparation Getting ready is the pressure this energy puts on you. Gate 62 is where it comes through: the drive to take something vast and give it a handle a person can hold, to know the facts, the small things, so that when the time comes nothing is missing. It puts a hard idea into plain, practical words, one step after another, so that others can use it. This is a voice of reason, grounded on what can be checked.

From outside it can look like fussing. The way it fails is over-preparing: the plan becomes more important than the thing it was for, the lists grow to keep the fear of not being ready at bay, and the present moment goes by unattended. People who carry this all their lives learn that they will know what they need to know when they need to know it, and that readiness was never in the plan. It was in trusting what arrives.
fields.tarot: Within the Ring of No Return, this code is the speaker. Its one sibling, UL 31, is the leader whose influence carries, and together they hold the throat's great initiation, the moment a voice begins to transmit truth and cannot take it back. Once a word of light is spoken it goes out into the world for good. There is no return. That is the name and the law of this small family. The Tarot reaches this card from two directions at once. The codon ring gives one Arcana, Judgement, the trumpet that wakes the dead. The two trigrams each give their own faces: Thunder above as the Tower and Judgement, the shock that breaks and the call that raises; Mountain below as the Hierophant and the Hermit, the keeper of the teaching and the one who carries the lamp alone. What they make together is a sound that breaks open the old, and a quiet that knows what to do with the space.
fields.body:
Your throat is where this energy is kept, and the reason is the hum. Everything you have ever said began as a small hum, two folds no longer than a fingernail fluttering a hundred times a second or more, and the mouth cut that hum into words on its way out. The voice is made in the throat; the words are made after. Before there were words there was only that sound, the sigh, the groan, and speech was learned by shaping it. Sitting low across the front of the throat is the thyroid, the gland whose whole day's work is a fleck, held within a narrow band, and that fleck sets the pace of everything in you.

Lay a hand flat on your throat and hum. The buzz under your palm is the thing itself. Now whisper the same word: the buzz is gone, because a whisper is breath through folds left ajar, and what you felt a moment ago is what every word of yours is built from. What the head is sure of can be talked out of it; what the body is sure of cannot, and the only thing the body is that sure of is love. That sureness has a substance in you, and the substance is tyrosine, one of the twenty small pieces you are built from, which your body makes for itself, so it is never missing. As your words get more exact, light comes through you in them, and what they are spoken through was made in you before you chose them, unasked.

Every word, once it has left you, does not come back, and the substance it was made of is shared with the part of you that leads other people by words. Open an old hard cheese and find the white grains that crunch: that is the thing itself, come out as the cheese dried over the years.

fields.essence: After something is finished, the questions begin. That is when you get curious about how the thing works, part by part, and whether it will hold. You go back over what everyone else has stopped looking at. There is always one more question behind the last one.
fields.glance:
After something is finished, the questions begin. That is when you get curious about how the thing works, part by part, and whether it will hold. You go back over what everyone else has stopped looking at. There is always one more question behind the last one.

Turned on the world around you, this curiosity finds the flaw everyone else missed and makes the thing work better. You take a theory or an engine apart piece by piece, and what you learn on the way is worth more than any one answer.

Some days the questions turn away from the thing you made and onto you, and you start doubting yourself. Tell someone you trust what is bothering you, and it starts to pass. Do not act in a hurry just to stop feeling unsure. Once everything is in its place, stay alert, because that is when a finished thing starts to slip. Some questions never get a final answer, and once you stop pushing for one, you can rest.
fields.iching:
The crossing is behind you, and what you set out to do is done. Every part of it is in its place. What is left is small, the settling in and the tidying up. This is where the danger lies. A thing in perfect order can move only one way, toward disorder. People stop watching once a matter is settled, and that is when they are most exposed. So the good fortune comes at the start of this time, and the disorder at its end.

Think about trouble while there is none, so you are ready when it comes. Keep going in the small things the way you did in the large ones. Think of the people who depend on what you have built, and put their good before your own. Know more than you use, and keep some of your strength back.

Your eyes and ears do the work now. The eyes go over what is finished. The ears catch the first drip of a leak. Sit the way someone sits when the day's work is done, with loose hands and open ears. Water over Fire is the hexagram of what comes after a thing is done. Fire is the clarity in you that sets each part of your work where it belongs. Water is the part of you that knows where the danger still is. The watching sits above the order because once a thing is done, keeping it is the work that is left. This hexagram has long been read as a pot of water over a flame. Tend both, and the water boils. Let either run wild, and it puts an end to the other. You are never more at risk than when everything is in its place. After Completion
fields.gene_keys:
Doubt Inquiry Truth Inquiry is doubt put to work. You can ask all your life without needing an answer to end it. A mind that fixes on one answer as the truth must defend it, and someone will always attack. An open mind has nothing to defend. It has the lightness of a child at play.

Ask deeply enough into anything and you find you are part of what you are looking at. From there the asking turns inward. What am I, asks the mind. What is love, asks the heart over and over, and it needs no final answer. A mind kept open grows soft, and an open mind opens the heart. Uncertainty is a pressure most people cannot bear. Whatever you settle, the doubt moves on to the next thing, and nothing ends it. So people take on a firm set of beliefs and hold them up against the doubt like a wall. Anyone who offers to end your uncertainty for good is selling you something false. Doubt is not the enemy. It turns harmful when you make it personal. Pushed out, it falls on the people closest to you. Turned in, it becomes doubt about yourself.

Here the mind works in the wrong order. Shown a sunset, it hears only its own words about it and is already thinking of tomorrow. Take a thing in first, and examine it after. Truth arrives when the question swallows the one asking it. You climbed for years toward an answer and wore yourself out on the way. At the top you found it had been at the foot all along, before you took a step. Trusted far enough, doubt turns out to be the truth itself, and the doubter dissolves into it.

Then there is rest, like sitting under a tree on a warm evening after walking all day. Every sigh brings you nearer to it, and so does every time your face softens. It is your plain state, closer than your own heartbeat. It is there at every step of the way.
fields.human_design: Curiosity Gate 63 sits at the top of your head and asks what comes next. It looks ahead to see which path will hold, what to follow and what to leave. It works by testing the next step before you take it, and it can tell a real teacher from a fake. Its fear is being wrong. Under the fear is a craving for certainty that no next step can meet.
fields.tarot: This energy asks, and asking is how every search begins. It belongs to a family of four, the Ring of Divinity, whose theme is suffering that opens you. UL 22, Treasure of the Way, carries grace. UL 36, Crystal Creation, carries the dark stretch that tests you. UL 37, Journey Home, carries the warmth of a family. This one carries the first question. Five of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
Sleep is the reason this energy is given to the pineal gland. The gland is the part of you that says the day is finished. About two hours before your usual bedtime it begins to tell your body that night has come. It says only that it is night, and leaves the sleeping to you. On some evenings your head lets go when it hears this, and on others the questions go on.

It keeps a clock that runs a little longer than a day. Each morning the first light through your eyes sets it again. Kept in dim light, a person drifts later day by day, and a morning outdoors puts it right. In animals that breed by the season, the length of its night is how the body knows the time of year. The doubt in you has a chemistry, and one substance in it is proline. Every protein in you is built from twenty pieces, and this is the one that turns the chain wherever it sits. When fear takes hold of doubt, heavy hormones go through you. Self-doubt taken all the way drains the body at that level, until your strength is simply gone.

Every person carries the same discomfort of not remembering who they truly are, and all people are equal in this one suffering. You share its chemistry with three other energies.

fields.essence: Before completion, a thing is almost made and still open to change. Imagination lives in that stretch, showing you the shape and colour of what you are making long before your hands get there. The pictures come whole and out of order, often in the middle of a change.
fields.glance:
Before completion, a thing is almost made and still open to change. Imagination lives in that stretch, showing you the shape and colour of what you are making long before your hands get there. The pictures come whole and out of order, often in the middle of a change.

Seeing the picture is half of this gift, and making it is the rest. That takes nerve, because what you make will change the life you have. You can ride imagination the way you would ride a wild horse, only as far as it agrees to go. It cannot be hurried: try to work it all out in your head and it shuts down. Leave it be, and it hands you the next piece as you build. So your life becomes a work in progress, and nothing in it is ever quite finished.

There are stretches when nothing will settle and no picture is clear. Your mind will want a reason and something to do. Every step you take just to end the not knowing makes it worse. What these stretches need is time. Given that, the pictures come back. Near the end, keep your eyes on the work in front of you, because the picture can make a thing feel done before it is.
fields.iching:
You are nearly across, and the last stretch is the one that decides it. Most of what you set out to do is done. The far bank is so close that watching your step now feels foolish. This is the moment the fox wets its tail. It acts as if it were across before it is, and loses the whole crossing at the last step.

What this time asks is that you check what is done before you call it done. Look at each part of what you have made and ask what it is really doing. Fire can warm water or boil it away, and water can cool a fire or put it out. The same two things help or harm depending on where they sit. So put each thing where it does its good.

Your feet are the last of you to cross, so keep your attention on them until you are out. Take the last step as carefully as the first. Wanting to be across is not the same as being across. Fire over Water is the hexagram of being nearly across. Fire is the clearness in you that tells one thing from another. Water is the risk you are still standing in. The clearness sits above the risk because you can see where you are going long before you are out of danger. That is why this hexagram has long been read as a young fox crossing a river. A step from the bank it thinks it is across, its tail goes in the water, and it cannot go on. Fire climbs and water sinks, so the two draw apart until each is set in its place. You can see clearly and still be in danger. Before Completion
fields.gene_keys:
Confusion Imagination Illumination Imagination begins when you stop trying to make the not knowing go away. The mind that was busy explaining goes quiet. The energy it was using comes back to you, and you start to make things with it. What arrives first is often the ache you were trying to avoid. Give it a shape in paint, in words or in a song, and it begins to change in your hands. Keep going, and the fears you drew at the start turn out to hold something good.

Imagination is also the end of copying. It goes where nobody has been, too quick and too wild to stop and explain itself. It will not keep to what you did last year. It asks you to let your life keep changing. Confusion is what a mind feels when everything in it has come loose and nothing has its order yet. It comes when what you knew about yourself stops holding. In itself it is full of what could be. It turns painful only when the mind tries to explain it. The mind wants a reason, then something to do, then the old order back.

Being unfinished is hard to bear, so the pull is to keep things as they were. A change that was trying to move you gets pressed back into its old shape. While it lasts you feel alone in it. Illumination is imagination that no longer belongs to you. The pictures and words still come, and they are made for whoever needs them. You stay empty while they pour through you.

Near such a person the eyes seem to shine and the room seems to shimmer. You hear such people only once you stop listening for the meaning. In the quiet between their words something true gets across.
fields.human_design: Confusion Gate 64 sits at the top of your head, where the question how begins. It fills with pictures: images, dreams and pieces of the past that arrive out of order. You can see them long before you can explain them. Along a straight line they read as a mess, which is why the gate is named for confusion. The pressure is to answer at once how each picture becomes real. Answered too early, that question shuts the dreaming down and leaves you tired and low.
fields.tarot: This energy turns a loose state into something new, and it does not do it alone. It belongs to a family of four called the Ring of Alchemy. UL 6 breaks down the walls between people, UL 40 builds that openness into communities, and UL 47 lets old ways change. This one opens a fresh set of possibilities. Four of the tarot's major cards, its Arcana, arrive through the ring and the two trigrams.
fields.body:
The pineal gland carries this energy, and the reason is light. It is the size of a grain of rice and sits in the middle of your head, where no daylight ever reaches. It learns whether the sun is up from your eyes, by a long road down into the neck and back. When the eyes report that the light has gone, it lets out the hormone of the dark and your body begins to slow. So a gland that lives in the dark keeps your day by light.

Sit in a dim room in the evening and within an hour or two you feel yourself grow heavy. Switch on a bright screen and the gland reads it as day, and the heaviness holds off. In some lizards its relative is a third eye under the skin of the crown, with a lens of its own. The light that lies hidden in you until it is ready to show has a substance, and it is glycine. It is the smallest of the twenty pieces your proteins are built from. Your body makes its own and takes in more from meat, fish and the jelly a cooled stock sets into. In your brain it sits at the gate where memory is laid down, and that gate will not open until glycine is in its seat.

You share this substance with three kin, and together the four change one state into the next. That change has long been told in colours. It starts black and passes through white and yellow to the red of gold. So whatever feels dark in you now is where that change begins.
